    Read the relevant operation/phase contract and verify target-release support.

column1: SRAP-24 | A validation reports the right error once, but the message remains after correction or appears on the wrong child. How would you debug it?
column2:
Short answer
I would inspect instance identity, field markers, parent paths and state-area handling in REPORTED, plus the corresponding FAILED entry where rejection is required. State messages represent current invalid state and need correct invalidation and revalidation; transition messages describe a particular operation. I would trace which validation triggers fire after correction and whether the UI is reading the right draft instance. An accurate message text cannot compensate for a wrong transactional key or stale state area.

Example
For an item delivery-date error, revalidate the affected item and clear the prior state appropriately before reporting the current result. Include a case where the item is deleted or moved out of the failing condition. Avoid blanket deletion of all messages, which can remove unrelated errors owned by other checks.

Avoid
Appending error text on every call without resetting its state area, or assuming REPORTED alone rejects a save.
RAP message lifecycle and correction

Follow the same child through an error and correction instead of treating a message as timeless text.
Explain it: Which identity and state area would you inspect when the old error remains?
Limit: Message lifetime and permitted state-message scenarios depend on active/draft and the supported operation contract.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • Which message should survive a round trip and which should not?
  • How would you preserve an unrelated validation's error while clearing this one?
Strong answer criteria
  • Correlates messages to transactional identity and fields
  • Manages state areas without erasing unrelated state
  • Separates messaging from operation rejection
Verification evidence
Test invalid-to-valid-to-invalid edits on two children, child deletion and activation; assert message paths, stale-message removal and correct save rejection.

Read and verify
  • SAP RAP state messages
    Compare persistent state-related messages with transition messages, instance identity and message invalidation.

column1: CDS-01 | What does ABAP CDS add to a SQL query?
column2:
Short answer
CDS defines reusable, semantically enriched data models in the ABAP repository. A model can describe elements, associations, annotations and access control, and can serve different consumers. SQL computes the result; CDS also supplies a stable model contract. Transactional behavior is added separately through RAP.

Example
For a sales-order list, expose keys, customer associations, currency semantics and authorized rows once. Several consumers can use that model without each recreating the joins.

Avoid
A CDS definition does not automatically implement create, update and delete operations.

Read and verify

    Check the entity type, provider contract and target-release restrictions.

column1: CDS-02 | What is the difference between a classic CDS view and a CDS view entity?
column2:
Short answer
A classic define view creates a CDS entity plus a separately named DDIC SQL view using AbapCatalog.sqlViewName. A define view entity avoids that separate DDIC SQL-view artifact and is the preferred choice for new supported scenarios. Choose according to the target release and consumer compatibility.

Example
During migration, inventory consumers that refer directly to the generated SQL-view name. Changing the source definition is not sufficient if those consumers still depend on the old object.

Avoid
Do not copy AbapCatalog.sqlViewName into a view entity or assume all older systems support view entities.

Read and verify

    Check the entity type, provider contract and target-release restrictions.

column1: CDS-03 | Association or join and how do you select cardinality?
column2:
Short answer
An association models a reusable relationship; a path expression can cause a join when the relationship is consumed. A join explicitly combines sources in the current query. Cardinality must describe the actual data relationship and ON condition. Wrong to-one assumptions can produce incorrect or optimizer-dependent results.

Example
For a flight-to-carrier association, an ON condition matching the carrier key can justify a to-one target cardinality if the data satisfies it. The flight's own identity is a separate question: it may require carrier, connection and flight date. Adding a date to the flight key does not establish the carrier relationship's cardinality. Test duplicate and missing target rows.

Avoid
Associations are not automatically faster than joins and do not enforce referential integrity.
CDS links and ownership

Items belong to the order BO; a partner reference crosses to an independently managed object.
Explain it: What breaks if a declared to-one relationship actually returns two partners?

column1: CDS-04 | Association versus composition in RAP?
column2:
Short answer
An association represents a relationship. A composition describes ownership within a RAP business-object tree, such as order and items. The root defines the aggregate boundary, with dependent locking and authorization where modeled. Exposed projections redirect associations and compositions to the corresponding projected entities.

Example
An item cannot be treated as an unrelated aggregate just because it has its own table. Explain create-by-association and what happens when the parent is deleted.

Avoid
Not every foreign key should become a composition; lifecycle ownership is the deciding factor.
CDS links and ownership

column1: CDS-05 | What do interface composite consumption and projection mean?
column2:
Short answer
Interface and consumption names describe modeling roles, while VDM basic, composite and consumption annotations describe a virtual data model convention. A RAP projection adapts one underlying entity for a use case under its provider contract. These labels are not interchangeable and do not themselves publish a service.

Example
Keep reusable business semantics below the consumer projection. Expose only needed fields and operations, and redirect associations consistently. Avoid adding layers whose only purpose is a naming pattern.

Avoid
A VDM composite annotation is neither a prerequisite for service binding nor permission to perform arbitrary joins in a RAP projection.

column1: CDS-06 | What are CDS abstract and custom entities?
column2:
Short answer
An abstract entity describes a structured type without a database result, often for action parameters, results or events. A custom entity represents a query model whose data is supplied by an ABAP implementation instead of a generated SQL query. Neither is an object-oriented abstract superclass.

Example
A Submit action may accept an abstract entity containing a comment. A custom query provider may assemble data from a remote service and must handle requested filters, paging and count.

Avoid
Do not describe an abstract entity as a BO that other CDS entities inherit and persist.

column1: CDS-07 | Does DCL on a base view automatically protect every higher view?
column2:
Short answer
No. Read authorization must be designed for each externally accessed CDS entity. A higher view can use its own access control with inherited conditions where supported. Merely adding AccessControl.authorizationCheck: #CHECK does not invent an access rule. RAP operation authorization is a separate concern.

Example
Test the projection used by the actual service with users from different company codes. Inspect the effective DCL and inheritance mapping, not just a protected lower-layer view.

Avoid
DCL on one layer does not automatically secure an arbitrary view-on-view stack.
CDS security boundaries

Review security where consumers enter the model, rather than assuming that lower layers protect every upper view.
Explain it: Which two tests prove that an exposed service rejects unauthorized access?
Limit: Authorization behavior depends on the access path and supported DCL inheritance mechanisms.

column1: CDS-08 | Where do UI annotations and value helps belong?
column2:
Short answer
Use metadata extensions for supported UI and consumption annotations when the model permits extensions. Keep core data semantics, such as amount and currency relationships, in the data model. Check annotation eligibility, layer precedence and release support rather than moving every annotation mechanically.

Example
A Fiori elements list can use line-item annotations and a currency-aware amount. A value help supports selection, but the backend must still validate submitted values and authorizations.

Avoid
UI.hidden and a value help are not security or data-integrity controls.
RAP contract stack

column1: CDS-09 | What is a virtual element and what are its limits?
column2:
Short answer
A virtual element is calculated in the application layer for a supported query scenario, commonly through a SADL calculation exit. It does not become a database column. Filtering, sorting and requesting the element need explicit supported handling and may differ by service and release.

Example
A display-only status text derived from an external source may fit. A field needed for efficient database filtering usually belongs in SQL/CDS or persistence instead. Fetch only needed calculation inputs.

Avoid
requestAtLeast is a UI request hint, not a universal guarantee that every consumer calculates a virtual element.

Explain it: Why can a correct calculation still yield a wrong page of results?

column1: CDS-10 | How do analytical CDS models differ from transactional models?
column2:
Short answer
Analytical models organize measures and dimensions, often around a cube and an analytical query or analytical projection. Transactional RAP models focus on identifiable instances and business operations. Aggregations must respect units, currencies and the query engine. One model is not automatically suitable for both purposes.

Example
Never sum EUR and USD amounts without the intended conversion or grouping. Confirm which analytical features the chosen protocol and consuming application actually execute.

Avoid
A VDM annotation or an OData $apply request alone does not guarantee correct analytical semantics.

column1: CDS-11 | How do CDS keys and database keys relate?
column2:
Short answer
A CDS key communicates entity identity to consumers but does not automatically enforce uniqueness in the query result. Database keys enforce uniqueness in persistence. Joins, missing key elements and aggregations can change result uniqueness. RAP and OData need stable, truly unique entity identities.

Example
If SFLIGHT rows differ by CARRID, CONNID and FLDATE, exposing only the first two as identity can merge or confuse rows in a client. Include the full business-relevant identity.

Avoid
Marking an element key does not remove duplicate rows.

column1: CDS-12 | Is a maintenance view a RAP view and how are defaults supplied?
column2:
Short answer
A classic DDIC maintenance view belongs to table/view maintenance, often with generated maintenance dialogs. A RAP application uses a CDS model and behavior instead. RAP defaults may be implemented with determinations or supported defaulting functions; field visibility depends on the chosen UI and metadata.

Example
First clarify whether the interviewer means SM30 maintenance or a Fiori RAP maintenance app. Then explain the appropriate maintenance events or RAP behavior mechanism.

Avoid

column1: MODEL-01 | A new consumption entity exposes orders outside the user's sales organization. The base CDS has DCL. What do you investigate?
column2:
Short answer
Trace the actual read entry point and its access control, including associations and alternative services. A protected base entity does not automatically confer equivalent protection on every higher entity. Define or inherit the intended restrictions through supported DCL constructs and mappings for the consumed entity. Keep operation authorization separate. The fix must preserve both authorized records and deliberate exceptions, rather than hiding the problem with a UI filter.

Example
Create two organizations with otherwise identical orders and use a restricted identity. Compare direct base consumption, the exposed projection and association navigation. Include count and value help: leaking a key or aggregate is still a data disclosure even when the main list looks correct.

Avoid
Do not add #CHECK and assume it creates a missing rule.
CDS security boundaries

Review security where consumers enter the model, rather than assuming that lower layers protect every upper view.
Explain it: Which two tests prove that an exposed service rejects unauthorized access?
Limit: Authorization behavior depends on the access path and supported DCL inheritance mechanisms.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • Which entry point actually evaluated DCL?
  • How would a field rename affect inherited restrictions?
Strong answer criteria
  • Traces the exposed read path
  • Defines restrictions at the correct boundary
  • Tests negative and positive identities
Verification evidence
Capture the real service responses for two organizational scopes, including navigation and counts.

Read and verify

    Verify the actual consumption path and include denied-user, filtering and boundary tests.

column1: MODEL-02 | An approver may update organization A. Can an update move an order from A to B using only existing-instance authorization?
column2:
Short answer
Authorization on the current instance can establish permission for its existing state, but that does not automatically approve the proposed target values. Treat the incoming organization change as a separate policy decision. Use supported prechecks and business validation/operation checks at appropriate points, with explicit handling of create and update. Derivations must not silently introduce a target scope that the caller was never allowed to choose.

Example
An order starts in A, so an existing-instance check succeeds. The payload proposes B. Test permitted A-to-A changes, forbidden A-to-B changes, initial values and batch requests. Ensure internal local-mode updates occur behind a verified public operation and still preserve business consistency.

Avoid
Do not equate authorization for the current object with authorization for any future object state.
Identity, authorization and feature control

Treat identity, business permission and contextual availability as separate checks.
Explain it: If Submit is disabled in Fiori, what happens when someone calls the service directly?
Limit: Static operation characteristics differ from dynamic instance/global feature checks.
Existing and proposed state authorization

Editing the current A instance and moving it into B are different authorization decisions. Partial input must be interpreted with existing state without treating omitted fields as explicit clears.
Explain it: Which state does each check inspect, and what happens if a determination changes the target scope?
Limit: A policy example, not a universal company-code rule. Implement through the target RAP scenario's supported hooks; prechecks do not replace the complete authorization model.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • What is checked for creation?
  • What happens if a determination changes the organization?
Strong answer criteria
  • Separates current and proposed state
  • Checks the public mutation boundary
  • Considers derived and bulk changes
Verification evidence
Demonstrate a rejected cross-scope update through the actual service with no unauthorized persisted change.

Read and verify
  • SAP RAP authorization control
    Verify the actual consumption path and include denied-user, filtering and boundary tests.

column1: MODEL-03 | A custom query returns only authorized rows but an unrestricted total count. Is it secure?
column2:
Short answer
No. Authorization must constrain the logical result before both counting and paging. A custom query provider owns the supported request semantics and cannot assume database-managed protections automatically cover remote or manually assembled data. Build one consistent authorized predicate and use it for data and count. Do not load all remote records into memory merely to hide unauthorized rows after an unrestricted count or aggregation.

Example
The caller may see five permitted orders while count reveals 900 hidden orders. Test zero-access users, count-only requests, filters, ordering and navigation. If the provider cannot securely support a requested aggregate or filter, reject it under a documented contract instead of returning a misleading result.

Avoid
Filtering only the displayed page leaves count, aggregates and existence checks exposed.
Filtering, paging and total count

Count and paging answer different questions. Stable ordering matters when the client requests successive pages.
Explain it: For this example, what count belongs beside a page of five records?
Limit: Provider-side execution order may be optimized while preserving request semantics.
Secure custom-query filtering, count, and page

The same authorized logical set contains IDs 2, 4, and 6. Counting it returns three; skipping one and taking two returns IDs 4 and 6 without revealing hidden B rows.
Explain it: What should a count-only request return, and what should happen if the filter cannot be represented safely?
Limit: The drawing specifies semantics, not a mandatory physical execution plan. A remote/custom provider must preserve equivalent authorization, filtering, count, and ordering behavior.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • How do you handle count-only requests?
  • What if the remote API cannot apply your authorization predicate?
Strong answer criteria
  • Uses one authorized result definition
  • Protects count and aggregates
  • Rejects unsupported semantics explicitly
Verification evidence
Use restricted identities and compare authorized data, count and aggregate responses over the same fixture.

Read and verify
  • SAP: Requesting and Setting Data or Count
    Handle data and count requests independently. Apply the same authorization and filtering to both; test count-only requests.

column1: MODEL-04 | A query-provider filter cannot be converted to simple ranges. A developer catches the exception and returns everything. What is the correction?
column2:
Short answer
Preserve the requested Boolean semantics or reject the unsupported filter clearly. Range conversion is not a universal representation of arbitrary nested AND/OR expressions and functions. Use a supported expression representation or another safe translation strategy appropriate to the provider. Combine user filters with mandatory authorization predicates independently, so a parsing failure cannot remove either restriction. Validate dynamic identifiers and values through supported APIs.

Example
Consider (region=A AND amount>100) OR (region=B AND urgent=true). Flattening this into independent region and amount ranges changes the result. Build fixtures that distinguish the intended expression from the flattened one, and include an unsupported-function request.

Avoid
A swallowed filter exception must not become an unrestricted selection.
Filtering, paging and total count

Count and paging answer different questions. Stable ordering matters when the client requests successive pages.
Explain it: For this example, what count belongs beside a page of five records?
Limit: Provider-side execution order may be optimized while preserving request semantics.
Secure custom-query filtering, count, and page

The same authorized logical set contains IDs 2, 4, and 6. Counting it returns three; skipping one and taking two returns IDs 4 and 6 without revealing hidden B rows.
Explain it: What should a count-only request return, and what should happen if the filter cannot be represented safely?
Limit: The drawing specifies semantics, not a mandatory physical execution plan. A remote/custom provider must preserve equivalent authorization, filtering, count, and ordering behavior.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • Can the backend express the same predicate?
  • How do mandatory authorization filters survive translation failure?
Strong answer criteria
  • Preserves AND/OR grouping
  • Separates mandatory restrictions
  • Returns an explicit unsupported-request outcome
Verification evidence
Compare expected row sets for nested filters and prove failure never broadens authorized access.

Read and verify
  • SAP: Implementing Filtering in an Unmanaged Query
    Check supported filter representations and conversion limitations. Unsupported input must not remove required user or authorization restrictions.

column1: MODEL-05 | A paged custom entity repeats some rows after an insertion. How would you make the contract predictable?
column2:
Short answer
Start with deterministic ordering that includes a unique tie-breaker; sorting only by a nonunique date is insufficient. Then distinguish deterministic order from snapshot consistency: concurrent inserts can still shift offset pages. Choose the supported continuation or consistency mechanism, or document the weaker browsing behavior if a snapshot is unnecessary. For an export requiring completeness, design a stable extraction boundary rather than assuming UI paging is a reliable bulk-transfer protocol.

Example
Twenty orders share a creation date. A new order is inserted between page requests. Test tied values, reverse sorting, deleted rows, empty pages and a count change. State whether the product requires an interactive current list or a reproducible export.

Avoid
Adding ORDER BY alone does not guarantee a frozen dataset across requests.
Filtering, paging and total count

Count and paging answer different questions. Stable ordering matters when the client requests successive pages.
Explain it: For this example, what count belongs beside a page of five records?
Limit: Provider-side execution order may be optimized while preserving request semantics.
Secure custom-query filtering, count, and page

The same authorized logical set contains IDs 2, 4, and 6. Counting it returns three; skipping one and taking two returns IDs 4 and 6 without revealing hidden B rows.
Explain it: What should a count-only request return, and what should happen if the filter cannot be represented safely?
Limit: The drawing specifies semantics, not a mandatory physical execution plan. A remote/custom provider must preserve equivalent authorization, filtering, count, and ordering behavior.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • What is the tie-breaker?
  • Does the use case require a snapshot or just stable ordering?
Strong answer criteria
  • Separates ordering from consistency
  • Chooses a contract for concurrent changes
  • Tests page boundaries with duplicate sort values
Verification evidence
Run successive requests while inserting and deleting records and verify the documented paging behavior.

Read and verify
  • SAP: Interface IF_RAP_QUERY_PAGING
    Distinguish offset, zero page size and PAGE_SIZE_UNLIMITED. The paging interface does not itself provide a cross-request snapshot.

column1: MODEL-06 | Adding a language-dependent text association doubles order totals. Would DISTINCT be a good fix?
column2:
Short answer
First identify the grain of the result and the actual join multiplicity. Check language, validity and other conditions that make the text association to-one or to-many. Declared cardinality is not data cleanup and can mislead optimization when false. Repair the relationship or aggregate at the correct grain before exposing the measure. DISTINCT can mask the symptom while retaining incorrect totals or discarding legitimate detail.

Example
One order worth 100 EUR joins two text rows and contributes 200 EUR to a sum. Add overlapping validity periods to the fixture as well as two languages. Verify both the detailed entity and the consuming analytical or list result.

Avoid
Do not fix an incorrect join by simply declaring a to-one cardinality.
SQL join multiplication

Joining two order headers to three items repeats order 10's total, inflating a naive sum from EUR 180 to EUR 280. For outer joins, matching conditions in ON can preserve unmatched left rows, while right-side conditions in WHERE can remove them.
Explain it: What is one row of this result supposed to represent? Where should a language filter go for optional text?
Limit: This is an inner-join example. WHERE and ON placement must follow intended semantics; neither DISTINCT nor SUM(DISTINCT amount) repairs every incorrect join or aggregation.
CDS links and ownership

Items belong to the order BO; a partner reference crosses to an independently managed object.
Explain it: What breaks if a declared to-one relationship actually returns two partners?
Limit: Composition semantics and generated operations still require the corresponding RAP model.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • What is one row supposed to represent?
  • Which data condition establishes uniqueness?
Strong answer criteria
  • Defines result grain
  • Proves association multiplicity
  • Checks the downstream measure
Verification evidence
Show expected rows and totals for multiple texts, missing texts and overlapping validity intervals.

Read and verify
  • SAP CDS modeling course
    Verify the actual consumption path and include denied-user, filtering and boundary tests.

column1: MODEL-07 | A CDS report sums 100 EUR and 100 USD into 200. What should the model and service do?
column2:
Short answer
Preserve amount/currency and quantity/unit semantics throughout the model. A sum is meaningful only within compatible units or after an explicitly defined conversion. Decide the target currency, rate type, date and rounding policy with the business owner. An annotation communicates semantics but does not, by itself, perform a correct conversion or make arbitrary aggregation valid. Verify how the actual analytical or transactional consumer interprets the exposed fields.

Example
Provide mixed currencies, a missing exchange rate and a value requiring rounding. A summary can group by currency or apply approved conversion, but must not silently combine incomparable values. Keep original values available where reconciliation requires them.

Avoid
Do not confuse semantic annotations with conversion logic.
Calculation placement and query semantics

Use the requirement to decide where a value must exist before filtering, ordering or aggregation.
Explain it: Why can a correct calculation still yield a wrong page of results?
Limit: Architecture alternatives, not a promise that all listed options are supported by each projection/custom provider.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • Which date determines the rate?
  • At which stage is rounding applied?
Strong answer criteria
  • Maintains unit semantics
  • Names the business conversion policy
  • Reconciles rounded and original values
Verification evidence
Compare expected totals for same-currency, mixed-currency and missing-rate fixtures.

Read and verify

    Verify the actual consumption path and include denied-user, filtering and boundary tests.

column1: MODEL-08 | A transactional projection needs a calculated field that its provider contract does not permit. How do you redesign it?
column2:
Short answer
Check the exact projection/provider-contract restrictions in the target release. Place permitted calculations in an appropriate underlying data model, expose a suitable read model, or use a supported virtual-element mechanism when its limitations fit. Do not turn a transactional projection into an arbitrary join solely to satisfy the UI. Preserve stable identity, behavior mapping, authorization and update semantics across the chosen design.

Example
The UI requests a derived risk band and wants to filter by it. A transient calculation may display correctly but fail server-side filtering. Decide whether the risk belongs in persistent business state, a database expression or a read-only enrichment, and test that consumer requirement.

Avoid
A field that displays in preview is not proof of a supported filterable transactional contract.
RAP contract stack

Read from the client down to storage, then explain what each artifact contributes.
Explain it: Where would you restrict the exposed operation set?
Limit: Conceptual layers; the exact artifact set depends on the scenario and release.

Use the requirement to decide where a value must exist before filtering, ordering or aggregation.
Explain it: Why can a correct calculation still yield a wrong page of results?
Limit: Architecture alternatives, not a promise that all listed options are supported by each projection/custom provider.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • Does the field participate in filtering or ordering?
  • Who owns recalculation when source data changes?
Strong answer criteria
  • Checks the provider contract
  • Preserves transactional identity
  • Designs for consumer query semantics
Verification evidence
Exercise read, filter, order and update against the intended binding on the target release.

column1: MODEL-09 | The business wants to sort a million-row list by a virtual element computed through a remote call. What would you propose?
column2:
Short answer
Challenge the requested access pattern before implementing row-by-row enrichment. A virtual element does not automatically support efficient database sorting, filtering or aggregation. Consider a permitted persistent read model with refresh rules, a supported pushdown calculation, or a bounded enrichment where sorting is not required. State freshness, failure and reconciliation requirements. Avoid moving an unbounded database workload into ABAP or remote calls.

Example
A risk score depends on a remote provider. Define how stale it may be and what the UI shows when the provider is unavailable. Compare query latency and result correctness with representative volumes; a fast demo using ten rows does not establish scalability.

Avoid
Do not claim that adding a virtual element automatically pushes its logic to HANA.
Calculation placement and query semantics

Use the requirement to decide where a value must exist before filtering, ordering or aggregation.
Explain it: Why can a correct calculation still yield a wrong page of results?
Limit: Architecture alternatives, not a promise that all listed options are supported by each projection/custom provider.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • What freshness is acceptable?
  • How many remote calls occur for one page and its count?

column1: MODEL-10 | Two rows in a service share the declared CDS key after a join. Why is this more than a display issue?
column2:
Short answer
Consumer identity must uniquely and stably distinguish each exposed instance. Declaring an element as key does not make a nonunique SQL result unique. Duplicate identities can corrupt navigation, client caching, selection and mutation targeting. Correct the data grain, join or composite key while assessing compatibility for existing consumers. If the current public identity is wrong, plan an explicit API transition rather than silently changing key meaning.

Example
An order-item service exposes only OrderId as key. Two items appear with the same identity and the UI targets the wrong item. Test read-by-key and navigation, not merely row count. Include repeated reads in different orders to reveal unstable client behavior.

Avoid
Do not hide duplicate-key rows with client-side deduplication.
SQL join multiplication

Joining two order headers to three items repeats order 10's total, inflating a naive sum from EUR 180 to EUR 280. For outer joins, matching conditions in ON can preserve unmatched left rows, while right-side conditions in WHERE can remove them.
Explain it: What is one row of this result supposed to represent? Where should a language filter go for optional text?
Limit: This is an inner-join example. WHERE and ON placement must follow intended semantics; neither DISTINCT nor SUM(DISTINCT amount) repairs every incorrect join or aggregation.
CDS links and ownership

Items belong to the order BO; a partner reference crosses to an independently managed object.
Explain it: What breaks if a declared to-one relationship actually returns two partners?
Limit: Composition semantics and generated operations still require the corresponding RAP model.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • Can the public key change compatibly?
  • Is the entity a business object instance or an aggregate?
Strong answer criteria
  • Proves key uniqueness at exposed grain
  • Explains consumer consequences
  • Plans compatible identity evolution
Verification evidence
Validate uniqueness, stable canonical URLs and correct read/update targeting for multiple child records.

Read and verify
  • SAP CDS modeling course
    Verify the actual consumption path and include denied-user, filtering and boundary tests.

column1: MODEL-11 | A value help reveals customer names that the order list hides. Where should the fix live?
column2:
Short answer
Treat the value-help entity and its text/navigation paths as separately consumed data contracts. Apply the required access restrictions and validate actual user identity and context. UI annotations can connect a value help but do not establish its authorization. Ensure the selected value is still validated at the write boundary because clients can submit a value without using the UI chooser.

Example
A restricted user opens customer search and learns names outside their organization. Test direct access to the value-help service, search/count behavior and a forged customer value in an order update. The read restriction and business consistency check solve related but distinct problems.

Avoid
Hiding the value-help control is not a backend security fix.
CDS security boundaries

Review security where consumers enter the model, rather than assuming that lower layers protect every upper view.
Explain it: Which two tests prove that an exposed service rejects unauthorized access?
Limit: Authorization behavior depends on the access path and supported DCL inheritance mechanisms.
Identity, authorization and feature control

Treat identity, business permission and contextual availability as separate checks.
Explain it: If Submit is disabled in Fiori, what happens when someone calls the service directly?
Limit: Static operation characteristics differ from dynamic instance/global feature checks.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • Can the entity be consumed directly?
  • What checks a value submitted outside Fiori?
Strong answer criteria
  • Protects auxiliary data exposure
  • Checks direct service access
  • Validates proposed business references

    Verify the actual consumption path and include denied-user, filtering and boundary tests.

column1: MODEL-12 | A batch job asks to use privileged EML because normal authorization rejects it. How do you evaluate the request?
column2:
Short answer
First establish the job identity, its legitimate business scope and whether normal authorization can represent that scope. Privileged access is a provider-enabled contract with specific bypass behavior, not a generic workaround. Review the defined authorization contexts, exposed entry points and caller trust boundary. If privilege is justified, narrowly encapsulate it, preserve remaining business checks and produce auditable evidence of who requested which effect.

Example
A repair job should reconcile one approved organizational scope, not become an unrestricted posting API. Test both the approved job path and attempts to reach the helper from an ordinary consumer. Confirm which checks are bypassed in the actual provider contract.

Avoid
Do not assume PRIVILEGED, IN LOCAL MODE and a technical user are equivalent.
Identity, authorization and feature control

Treat identity, business permission and contextual availability as separate checks.
Explain it: If Submit is disabled in Fiori, what happens when someone calls the service directly?
Limit: Static operation characteristics differ from dynamic instance/global feature checks.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • Which authorization context is disabled?
  • Why cannot ordinary scoped authorization satisfy the requirement?
Strong answer criteria
  • Requires a provider-supported privilege contract
  • Limits the trusted entry point
  • Retains business checks and auditability
Verification evidence
Review privilege configuration and demonstrate allowed repair plus rejected unauthorized invocation.

    Verify the actual consumption path and include denied-user, filtering and boundary tests.

column1: MODEL-13 | A developer uses IN LOCAL MODE in a helper to avoid feature checks. What makes the helper safe or unsafe?
column2:
Short answer
Locate the helper within its own BO implementation and trace every public operation that can reach it. Local mode supports internal state maintenance and bypasses defined checks depending on the operation; it does not authorize arbitrary external business requests or erase transactional constraints. Ensure public inputs have already been checked and that internal changes preserve invariants. Review cross-BO calls under their own contracts.

Example
A determination legitimately updates a derived readonly amount. The same helper becomes unsafe if a public action forwards arbitrary caller values to it. Test that the derived field cannot be controlled indirectly through a newly added action parameter.

Avoid
Do not fix missing authorization by routing all work through local mode.
Identity, authorization and feature control

Treat identity, business permission and contextual availability as separate checks.
Explain it: If Submit is disabled in Fiori, what happens when someone calls the service directly?
Limit: Static operation characteristics differ from dynamic instance/global feature checks.
Existing and proposed state authorization

Editing the current A instance and moving it into B are different authorization decisions. Partial input must be interpreted with existing state without treating omitted fields as explicit clears.
Explain it: Which state does each check inspect, and what happens if a determination changes the target scope?
Limit: A policy example, not a universal company-code rule. Implement through the target RAP scenario's supported hooks; prechecks do not replace the complete authorization model.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • Which controls does this specific operation bypass?
  • Can a caller influence the supposedly derived values?
Strong answer criteria
  • Traces trust from public input
  • Confines internal state changes
  • Distinguishes own-BO and cross-BO access
Verification evidence
Use adversarial action inputs and verify that only approved derivations reach readonly or protected fields.

column1: MODEL-14 | A CDS unit test passes, but the same entity leaks data for a restricted user. What may the test be missing?
column2:
Short answer
Inspect the test environment and access-control configuration. A test focused on relational logic with CDS doubles may intentionally isolate or disable access control; it is not automatically an authorization test. Enable the supported access-control testing mechanism with meaningful role data where available, and add real service tests under restricted identities. Keep query-correctness evidence separate from security evidence.

Example
One test proves the join returns three rows. Add fixtures for no authorization and two distinct scopes, then ensure the test actually evaluates DCL. A final service test also verifies binding, identity propagation and the real consumed entity.

Avoid
A green database-double test does not prove deployed authorization.
CDS security boundaries

Review security where consumers enter the model, rather than assuming that lower layers protect every upper view.
Explain it: Which two tests prove that an exposed service rejects unauthorized access?
Limit: Authorization behavior depends on the access path and supported DCL inheritance mechanisms.
Real behavior under test and dependency doubles

Two deliberately different inputs exercise the real Submit rule while a separate limit-provider dependency is controlled. Assertions inspect state and response identity, not only execution coverage.
Explain it: If the account-assignment rejection is removed, which test fails? What evidence remains missing after these tests pass?
Limit: The fixture is conceptual and not an executed ABAP Unit result. Framework double support and persistence setup depend on the target release and test boundary.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • Is DCL enabled in the test environment?
  • Which real identity is used by the service?
Strong answer criteria
  • Inspects double behavior
  • Adds denied and scoped authorization cases
  • Separates unit and deployed evidence
Verification evidence
Show test configuration plus restricted-user service results; do not infer one from the other.

Read and verify
  • SAP CDS access-control tests
    Verify the actual consumption path and include denied-user, filtering and boundary tests.

column1: MODEL-15 | An integration user can access all tenants or clients through a custom read provider. What boundaries must be reviewed?
column2:
Short answer
Separate technical client handling, tenant isolation, business authorization and remote credentials. Standard data-access behavior does not automatically protect arbitrary remote calls or custom assembled datasets. Avoid accepting unrestricted client/tenant selectors from untrusted request input. Use supported tenant-aware access and configuration, enforce business scope and test identity propagation. The exact tenant model differs by environment and must be established explicitly.

Example
A provider forwards an incoming company or tenant parameter to a privileged remote destination. Even if the local CDS looks restricted, the remote response may cross the intended boundary. Test two scopes with overlapping business IDs and inspect both request construction and returned data.

Avoid
Do not treat a client field, a destination name or authentication alone as complete tenant isolation.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • Who controls the remote tenant selector?
  • Which identity does the remote system evaluate?
Strong answer criteria
  • Separates technical and business scope
  • Constrains untrusted selectors
  • Checks end-to-end identity propagation
Verification evidence
Run cross-scope negative tests and review the permitted communication configuration without exposing secrets.

Read and verify
  • SAP RAP authorization control
    Verify the actual consumption path and include denied-user, filtering and boundary tests.

column1: MODEL-16 | A projection hides an operation, but another consumer can still call the base BO. Is hiding sufficient?
column2:
Short answer
Projection restrictions define a consumer-facing operation surface, not a universal revocation of the underlying capability. Review who can consume the base BO or another released interface, and enforce security at the appropriate behavior boundary. Keep public API release, package visibility and operation authorization aligned. Feature control can improve availability feedback but cannot replace authorization for alternative entry points.

Example
A UI projection excludes Delete while a background consumer uses a broader local BO interface. Decide whether that capability is intentional for the background role. Test direct access to every supported mutation path using an unauthorized identity.

Avoid
Do not use the UI service shape as the only security policy.
RAP contract stack

Read from the client down to storage, then explain what each artifact contributes.
Explain it: Where would you restrict the exposed operation set?
Limit: Conceptual layers; the exact artifact set depends on the scenario and release.
CDS security boundaries

Review security where consumers enter the model, rather than assuming that lower layers protect every upper view.
Explain it: Which two tests prove that an exposed service rejects unauthorized access?
Limit: Authorization behavior depends on the access path and supported DCL inheritance mechanisms.
Identity, authorization and feature control

Treat identity, business permission and contextual availability as separate checks.
Explain it: If Submit is disabled in Fiori, what happens when someone calls the service directly?

Existing and proposed state authorization

Editing the current A instance and moving it into B are different authorization decisions. Partial input must be interpreted with existing state without treating omitted fields as explicit clears.
Explain it: Which state does each check inspect, and what happens if a determination changes the target scope?
Limit: A policy example, not a universal company-code rule. Implement through the target RAP scenario's supported hooks; prechecks do not replace the complete authorization model.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • Which consumers are permitted to use the base contract?
  • Where does the decisive permission check execute?
Strong answer criteria
  • Inventories alternate entry points
  • Separates surface restriction from permission
  • Tests local and remote consumers
Verification evidence
Provide a consumer/operation/identity matrix and evidence of denied mutation through each exposed path.

column1: MODEL-17 | A released entity gains a new field that is expensive and sensitive. Is an additive change automatically safe?
column2:
Short answer
Not necessarily. Check default projection, serialization, authorization, query cost and consumers that interpret metadata or request broad selections. Preserve compatibility while deciding whether the field belongs in the same public contract or a more restricted projection. Avoid unexpected remote enrichment or large payload growth on existing list requests. Verify the relevant release contract and supported evolution rules before shipping.

Example
A new personal-data field is included by broad selects and exports. Another computed field adds one remote call per row. Existing callers did not change, but privacy and latency did. Test default reads, explicit selection, metadata-driven UIs and restricted identities.

Avoid
Do not assess compatibility using only whether old source code still compiles.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • Does an existing broad select expose it?
  • How does it affect authorization and request cost?
Strong answer criteria
  • Assesses semantic and operational compatibility
  • Controls default exposure
  • Tests unchanged consumers
Verification evidence
Compare old/new payloads, access results and latency for representative existing requests.

Read and verify
  • SAP BO interfaces
    Verify the actual consumption path and include denied-user, filtering and boundary tests.

column1: MODEL-18 | An analytical requirement is added to a transactional BO. Would you put every aggregate into its projection?
column2:
Short answer
Choose a read model appropriate to the analytical grain and consumer rather than distorting transactional identity and behavior. Reuse trustworthy underlying semantics where suitable, then define aggregation, currency, authorization and freshness deliberately. Keep transactional mutations on the BO contract. A separate analytical model may be justified, but avoid duplicating business rules without an ownership and consistency plan.

Example
An approval object needs both item editing and monthly spend by organization. The monthly aggregate is not the same entity identity as an editable item. Compare whether live calculation meets latency or whether a reconciled read model is necessary.

Avoid
Do not make an aggregate writable merely because its source is a transactional BO.
SQL join multiplication

Joining two order headers to three items repeats order 10's total, inflating a naive sum from EUR 180 to EUR 280. For outer joins, matching conditions in ON can preserve unmatched left rows, while right-side conditions in WHERE can remove them.
Explain it: What is one row of this result supposed to represent? Where should a language filter go for optional text?
Limit: This is an inner-join example. WHERE and ON placement must follow intended semantics; neither DISTINCT nor SUM(DISTINCT amount) repairs every incorrect join or aggregation.
Calculation placement and query semantics

Use the requirement to decide where a value must exist before filtering, ordering or aggregation.
Explain it: Why can a correct calculation still yield a wrong page of results?
Limit: Architecture alternatives, not a promise that all listed options are supported by each projection/custom provider.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • What is the aggregate grain?
  • How are authorization and currency preserved across the models?
Strong answer criteria
  • Separates transaction and analytical identity
  • Reuses semantics intentionally
  • Defines freshness and reconciliation
Verification evidence
Reconcile grouped totals to authorized transactional fixtures and validate the intended analytical consumer.

Read and verify
  • SAP analytical projection modeling
    Verify the actual consumption path and include denied-user, filtering and boundary tests.

column1: ADV-01 | How do pessimistic locks and ETags complement each other?
column2:
Short answer
A pessimistic lock prevents conflicting processing for a time. An ETag detects whether the version a client read is still current when it writes. RAP defines lock ownership and optimistic concurrency through behavior. Draft scenarios also need total-ETag handling for relevant active-data changes.

Example
Two users read a request. After one saves, the other's stale If-Match must not silently overwrite it. A draft lock and an active-data version check solve different parts of this problem.

Avoid
Locking and logging are different concepts; an ETag is not a log and does not reserve the object.
Draft lifecycle

Follow edit, activate and discard for an existing active object, then explain how a new-object draft differs.
Explain it: What remains after discarding an edit draft? What if activation fails?
Limit: Schematic state transitions; draft actions and supported flows depend on the BO and consumer.
Two ETag boundaries

The left side tests a conditional entity update; the right tests the active-state basis of a resumed draft.
Explain it: Why does testing one entity ETag not prove the draft total-ETag implementation?
Limit: ETags are opaque. Verify lock expiry, relevant child changes and generated behavior on the actual system.
Two editors and one version: an illustrated story

Alice and Ben read version 7. Alice updates successfully, producing version 8. Ben must not overwrite that newer state using the stale version 7 precondition.
Explain it: Why should the client refresh and resolve the conflict instead of blindly retrying its old payload?
Limit: Version numbers are illustrative. Real ETags are opaque validators; a failed If-Match precondition commonly returns HTTP 412. This is optimistic concurrency, not a pessimistic lock.

Read and verify
  • SAP draft concept
    Check the supported RAP behavior and consumer/version contract.

column1: ADV-02 | Global authorization instance authorization or feature control?
column2:
Short answer
Global authorization checks permissions independent of a specific instance. Instance authorization considers an instance's context. Feature control enables operations or fields according to business state. UI availability and feature control help consumers, but authorization must enforce who may perform the operation.

Example
A submitted request may be readonly for everyone as a feature rule; approval may additionally require the assigned approver's authority. Test a direct API request as well as the disabled UI button.

Avoid
Hiding or disabling a button is not an authorization check.
CDS security boundaries

Review security where consumers enter the model, rather than assuming that lower layers protect every upper view.
Explain it: Which two tests prove that an exposed service rejects unauthorized access?
Limit: Authorization behavior depends on the access path and supported DCL inheritance mechanisms.
Identity, authorization and feature control

Treat identity, business permission and contextual availability as separate checks.
Explain it: If Submit is disabled in Fiori, what happens when someone calls the service directly?
Limit: Static operation characteristics differ from dynamic instance/global feature checks.

Read and verify

    Check the supported RAP behavior and consumer/version contract.

column1: ADV-03 | What does authorization none on an action mean?
column2:
Short answer
Where supported, authorization: none exempts that action from the RAP authorization checks specified for it. It does not remove authentication at the service boundary or every authorization check in downstream code. Use it only with a deliberate security model and the exact supported behavior syntax.

Example
An action that needs no object-specific authorization may still operate through an authenticated service and call another API that performs its own checks. Document why the exemption is justified.

Avoid
Do not propose it as a universal fix for authorization errors or expose a sensitive action by accident.
Identity, authorization and feature control

Treat identity, business permission and contextual availability as separate checks.
Explain it: If Submit is disabled in Fiori, what happens when someone calls the service directly?
Limit: Static operation characteristics differ from dynamic instance/global feature checks.

Read and verify
  • SAP Learning on authorization
    Check the supported RAP behavior and consumer/version contract.

column1: ADV-04 | Instance static and factory actions?
column2:
Short answer
An instance action operates on identified instances. A static action belongs to the entity without requiring an existing instance. A factory action creates instances and returns the appropriate creation mapping. Their inputs, results and identity handling differ, so choose according to the business operation.

Example
Approve acts on a request, CalculatePreview may be static, and CopyRequest can be a factory action. A normal instance action returning $self is not automatically a factory action.

Avoid
Static does not mean a static ABAP method that can ignore RAP identity and response contracts.
RAP hook responsibilities

Read each card as a separate design question; this is not an execution sequence.
Explain it: Where would you derive a total, reject an invalid input and implement Submit?
Limit: Check scenario and release support; do not rely on an undocumented ordering of independent hooks.

Read and verify
  • SAP action definitions
    Check the supported RAP behavior and consumer/version contract.

column1: ADV-05 | How do action parameters and results work?
column2:
Short answer
Define a supported parameter and result shape in the behavior contract, often using a CDS abstract entity for structured input. Implement the generated handler signature and populate the requested result and response structures correctly. Cardinality and binding to instances are part of the contract.

Example
Submit may accept a comment; CalculatePreview may return totals without persisting an object. The UI may generate a dialog from the parameter metadata, subject to consumer support.

Avoid
Parameters are not defined by putting an action inside an abstract entity.
RAP hook responsibilities

Read each card as a separate design question; this is not an execution sequence.
Explain it: Where would you derive a total, reject an invalid input and implement Submit?
Limit: Check scenario and release support; do not rely on an undocumented ordering of independent hooks.

column1: ADV-06 | What is augmentation and how does it differ from additional save?
column2:
Short answer
Augmentation adapts supported modifying operations at a RAP projection boundary, allowing projection-specific input to be enriched or translated. Additional save adds persistence-related work alongside a managed save scenario. They run for different purposes and are not interchangeable hooks.

Example
A projection may transform consumer-specific input into changes understood by the underlying BO. Audit records associated with managed persistence may instead need an additional-save design compatible with the transaction.

Avoid
Augmentation is not a generic before-save hook for copying every virtual element into a table.
Augmentation versus additional save

Locate the input transformation and persistence supplement on the same conceptual timeline.
Explain it: Why would writing an audit row not make augmentation the right save hook?
Limit: The arrow is conceptual; availability, supported fields and trigger details depend on the target RAP release.

    Check the supported RAP behavior and consumer/version contract.

column1: ADV-07 | What are side effects in a RAP UI?
column2:
Short answer
Side-effect metadata tells a capable consumer which values, messages or permissions to refresh after a relevant change or action. The backend must still compute correct results; the metadata coordinates refresh behavior. Backend release, service metadata and SAPUI5 support determine which declarations are available.

Example
After changing quantity, refresh total amount and action availability. Verify network requests and the displayed values, especially after an action result or draft update.

Avoid
A side-effect declaration does not implement the calculation or force all non-UI consumers to issue extra reads.
Side effects and stale UI diagnosis

Use the observed backend value to choose the next debugging branch.
Explain it: What request proves that the consumer refreshed the calculated total?
Limit: Consumer and metadata support are release-dependent; a valid backend side effect is not proof that every client processes it.

Read and verify

    Read the field/action trigger and refresh-target contract; verify the actual UI consumer support.

column1: ADV-08 | State messages versus transition messages?
column2:
Short answer
A state message describes an invalid state of an instance and may persist in a supported draft scenario until revalidated. A transition message relates to the current operation or request. Use the appropriate state area and instance or field references and clear obsolete state correctly.

Example
A missing mandatory date can remain highlighted while editing a draft. A successful one-time submission notification should not reappear forever as a stale state error.

Avoid
Every error should not be stored as a persistent state message, and REPORTED alone does not block saving.
Draft lifecycle

Follow edit, activate and discard for an existing active object, then explain how a new-object draft differs.
Explain it: What remains after discarding an edit draft? What if activation fails?
Limit: Schematic state transitions; draft actions and supported flows depend on the BO and consumer.
RAP message lifecycle and correction

Follow the same child through an error and correction instead of treating a message as timeless text.
Explain it: Which identity and state area would you inspect when the old error remains?
Limit: Message lifetime and permitted state-message scenarios depend on active/draft and the supported operation contract.

Read and verify
  • SAP RAP state messages
    Compare persistent state-related messages with transition messages, instance identity and message invalidation.

column1: ADV-09 | Service definition versus binding and UI versus Web API?
column2:
Short answer
A service definition selects exposed entities and names. A binding attaches a protocol and service type, such as OData V4 UI or Web API. UI services support relevant UI semantics; Web APIs target programmatic consumers. Activation, local publication, authorization and deployment are separate concerns.

Example
Choose the consumer first, then inspect generated metadata and test the actual endpoint. A local ADT preview is useful, but transport and production communication setup still need validation.

Avoid
VDM.viewType: #COMPOSITE neither creates nor activates a service binding.
RAP contract stack

Read from the client down to storage, then explain what each artifact contributes.
Explain it: Where would you restrict the exposed operation set?
Limit: Conceptual layers; the exact artifact set depends on the scenario and release.

Read and verify
  • SAP service binding documentation
    Check the supported RAP behavior and consumer/version contract.

column1: ADV-10 | What must a custom query provider implement?
column2:
Short answer
A provider supplies data according to the requested query contract, including applicable filtering, ordering, paging, selected elements and total count. It should process only requested information and preserve authorization. Unsupported query options must be handled deliberately. Remote sources add latency, consistency and error-mapping concerns.

Example
Handle data and total-count requests independently: a count-only request must not depend on a data-request branch. Compute count over the same authorized, filtered result before paging, and use deterministic ordering for data. A zero page size requests no rows; distinguish it from IF_RAP_QUERY_PAGING=>PAGE_SIZE_UNLIMITED. Do not accidentally translate zero into an unrestricted SQL read. Test count-only, empty-page and unlimited requests as well as ordinary pages.

Avoid
Returning any internal table is not a correct implementation of IF_RAP_QUERY_PROVIDER.
Filtering, paging and total count

Count and paging answer different questions. Stable ordering matters when the client requests successive pages.
Explain it: For this example, what count belongs beside a page of five records?
Limit: Provider-side execution order may be optimized while preserving request semantics.

Read and verify
  • SAP: Implementing an Unmanaged Query
    Check the supported request contract and target release. Scenario-specific bulk access and caching decisions still need their own correctness and performance evidence.
  • SAP: Requesting and Setting Data or Count
    Handle data and count requests independently. Apply the same authorization and filtering to both; test count-only requests.
  • SAP: Interface IF_RAP_QUERY_PAGING
    Distinguish offset, zero page size and PAGE_SIZE_UNLIMITED. The paging interface does not itself provide a cross-request snapshot.

column1: ADV-11 | How do RAP business events differ from ABAP Objects events?
column2:
Short answer
ABAP Objects events use event handlers within the ABAP execution context. RAP business events describe business occurrences under RAP's event contract; supported local or remote consumption has its own lifecycle. Remote enterprise events require configured infrastructure and transactional publication, with retry and idempotency designed explicitly.

Example
Use an integration event after a request is durably submitted. A remote consumer should tolerate duplicate delivery and should not approve a request merely because it received an uncommitted local callback.

Avoid
Do not collapse every locally consumed RAP event into synchronous SET HANDLER semantics or promise universal ordering.
Duplicate events and stale approvals

The event identity and current business state decide whether to apply, ignore or reject the request.
Explain it: Two consumers process the same event simultaneously: what prevents a double effect?
Limit: Exact transactional deduplication mechanisms depend on the chosen infrastructure.

Read and verify
  • SAP: Develop Business Events
    Release-specific RAP event documentation. Check the event definition, publication and supported consumption contract on the target release; infrastructure and delivery semantics need separate verification.

column1: ADV-12 | How do you extend an existing RAP BO safely?
column2:
Short answer
Inspect its released extension contract and supported extension points before adding fields or behavior. Check model, projection, metadata, authorization, save and service implications. Extension support depends on the BO and release; an accessible source object is not necessarily released for extension.

Example
For an extra approval reference, verify persistence extension, exposure, validation, update behavior and consumer compatibility end to end. Test the standard flow without the new field as well.

Avoid
Being able to create a CDS extension does not prove every BO behavior or API contract is extensible.

Read and verify
  • SAP: RAP Extensibility Enablement
    Verify explicit extensibility enablement and the released extension contract for each affected layer on the target release.

column1: ADV-13 | How do static and dynamic feature controls differ?
column2:
Short answer
Static restrictions are declared in the behavior definition, for example a readonly or mandatory field. Dynamic controls determine supported operation or field availability from global or instance context. They express business availability, while authorization remains separate. Check which controls the operation and target release support.

Example
An approved request may dynamically forbid editing. A generated UUID may be statically readonly. Global and instance feature control cannot both be declared for the same operation; choose the applicable contract and implement its generated handler.

Avoid
A dynamic UI state does not prove security, and mandatory metadata does not replace all backend business validations.
Identity, authorization and feature control

Treat identity, business permission and contextual availability as separate checks.
Explain it: If Submit is disabled in Fiori, what happens when someone calls the service directly?
Limit: Static operation characteristics differ from dynamic instance/global feature checks.

Read and verify
  • SAP feature control
    Check the supported RAP behavior and consumer/version contract.

column1: OPS-01 | How would you test a Submit action without replacing the business object you are supposed to verify?
column2:
Short answer
Keep the Submit implementation and its relevant BO behavior real. Isolate true dependencies such as database tables, external service adapters or other BOs using the appropriate supported doubles. Drive the operation through a meaningful boundary, often EML, and assert state changes, failures and messages. A double of the very action under test would prove the configured double response rather than the business rule.

Example
A purchase request can be submitted only when every item has an account assignment. Test a valid request and a missing assignment, including persisted outcome after the supported save boundary. If another BO supplies a limit, double that dependency and vary its response.

Avoid
Do not label a test of a mocked Submit response as a test of Submit.
Testing scope and evidence

The widening base suggests many focused checks, but there is no mandatory numerical ratio.
Explain it: Which risk remains after an ABAP Unit test with doubles passes?
Limit: Conceptual coverage map, not a count of tests actually run in SAP.

column1: OPS-03 | A bulk EML action processes ten requests and rejects two. What should its test assert?

column1: OPS-04 | A draft test passes when run alone but fails after another test. What would you inspect?
column2:

column1: OPS-05 | How do you prove optimistic concurrency rather than merely calling the same update twice?
column2:
Short answer
Use independent consumers or sessions that read the same initial version, then perform conflicting updates in a controlled order. Assert that the first permitted write succeeds and the stale second precondition is rejected without lost data. For draft, separately test the exclusive-lock and total-ETag situations. A sequential test that rereads after every update never exercises a stale writer.

Example
Alice and Ben read the same entity instance with its entity ETag. Alice updates that instance successfully; Ben submits an update to that same instance using the stale ETag and must not overwrite it. Separately test child-only active changes against the configured draft total ETag when resuming an expired draft lock. Keep entity-level conditional update and draft-resume concurrency assertions distinct.

Avoid
Two updates in one shared transaction are not a realistic two-user concurrency test.
Two ETag boundaries

The left side tests a conditional entity update; the right tests the active-state basis of a resumed draft.
Explain it: Why does testing one entity ETag not prove the draft total-ETag implementation?
Limit: ETags are opaque. Verify lock expiry, relevant child changes and generated behavior on the actual system.
Two editors and one version: an illustrated story

Alice and Ben read version 7. Alice updates successfully, producing version 8. Ben must not overwrite that newer state using the stale version 7 precondition.
Explain it: Why should the client refresh and resolve the conflict instead of blindly retrying its old payload?
Limit: Version numbers are illustrative. Real ETags are opaque validators; a failed If-Match precondition commonly returns HTTP 412. This is optimistic concurrency, not a pessimistic lock.

  • Which field protects the whole draft object?

column1: OPS-07 | A RAP list becomes slow after enabling count and expanding children. What do you measure first?
column2:

Use available traces and representative parameters to measure rows, calls, database time and application time. Optimize the observed bottleneck while preserving query and security semantics. A 20-row page triggers an expensive count across millions of authorized records plus child expansion. Removing a SELECT from one handler may be irrelevant. Compare page-only, count-only and expanded requests, including a restricted user whose authorization predicate changes the plan.

column1: OPS-08 | A custom entity calls a remote API once for every returned row. How would you remove the N+1 pattern?
column2:
Short answer

One list page of 50 items makes 51 remote calls. A bulk endpoint can retrieve the needed reference data in one request, but may return partial failures. Test missing references, duplicate keys and service throttling, not only the happy-path call count.

column1: OPS-11 | A remote approval succeeded, but the RAP caller timed out. How should an operator recover?
column2:
Short answer
Treat the outcome as uncertain until reconciled using stable correlation. Do not blindly resubmit a non-idempotent business action. Identify which system owns each committed effect and use the documented status query, idempotency contract or compensation process. Preserve a durable recovery record and route unresolved cases to an owner. A local rollback cannot erase a remote commit.

Example
The remote workflow created an approval instance, but its response was lost. A retry should find or reuse that instance rather than create another. Include a later duplicate callback and an approval referring to an outdated local version.

A timeout is not evidence that the other system performed no work.

The remote commit belongs to another system, so local failure needs an explicit recovery strategy.

The event identity and current business state decide whether to apply, ignore or reject the request.

Limit: Exact transactional deduplication mechanisms depend on the chosen infrastructure.

The local application durably records intent before separately owned delivery. The remote payment commits, but its reply is lost; recovery must identify the existing effect through REQ-42.
Explain it: How do you distinguish an unprocessed request from a committed payment whose response never arrived?
Limit: The delivery and idempotency mechanisms are design requirements, not automatic guarantees from HTTP or RAP. This example does not claim distributed atomicity.

column1: ABAP-01 | How do you choose between standard, sorted, and hashed internal tables?
column2:
Short answer
I choose from the access pattern. A standard table suits indexed access and sequential processing. A sorted table maintains key order and supports efficient key and range access. A hashed table suits repeated complete-key lookup and requires a unique primary key. I also consider write volume, memory, and secondary keys before choosing.

Example
For an order import, lt_orders can be a standard table when input order matters. A hashed lookup by unique order ID avoids repeated linear scans. A sorted table by customer and order ID supports processing each customer's contiguous group.

Avoid
A hashed primary key is unique; that does not mean every field value must be unique or that arbitrary partial-key searches are constant time.
Internal table lookup

A free-key linear search, an ordered lookup, and a complete hashed-key lookup find the same record through different access paths.
Explain it: What changes if I need all rows in a key range, or preserve input order?
Limit: A standard table can use secondary keys; a hash lookup requires a suitable complete key. Hash storage and probe order are schematic, not SAP implementation guarantees.

column1: ABAP-02 | What are primary, secondary, default, and empty internal table keys?

A standard table can preserve arrival order and still expose a sorted secondary key for customer access. I name the secondary key in the access when needed, and measure whether its repeated-read benefit justifies the overhead of frequent inserts or changes.

column1: ABAP-03 | When is BINARY SEARCH correct, and how do table expressions handle missing rows?

If absence means an optional description, VALUE with OPTIONAL may be appropriate. If an order must exist, returning an initial structure would hide a defect. When I need the row, I avoid an existence check followed by a second identical lookup.

Two fields can share a technical domain while using different data elements because their business meanings and labels differ. A reusable table type might describe a collection of request items, but declaring that type does not create database records.

column1: ABAP-07 | How do you explain an SAP LUW versus a database LUW?
column2:
Short answer
A database LUW is the database transaction completed by a database commit or rollback. An SAP LUW groups a business change across application processing, potentially spanning multiple database LUWs in classic dialog processing. The application coordinates consistency using appropriate persistence, update mechanisms, and logical locks. The transaction owner decides when the business operation is complete.

Example
In a classic document change, user interaction can span dialog steps. Holding ordinary database locks across that entire interaction is unsuitable, so the application uses SAP enqueue locks and a defined save process. RAP instead provides a framework-controlled transaction and save sequence.

column1: ABAP-08 | Who should issue COMMIT WORK, and what does AND WAIT guarantee?
column2:
Short answer

Neither form guarantees that every asynchronous follow-up in the landscape has completed successfully.

A reusable posting service called within a larger business operation must respect the caller's transaction contract. In RAP behavior code I do not insert COMMIT WORK or BAPI_TRANSACTION_COMMIT; framework restrictions and the actual legacy API's commit behavior must be checked.

column1: ABAP-10 | How do you choose and propagate class-based exceptions?
column2:
Short answer
I use CX_STATIC_CHECK for an explicit recoverable failure contract, CX_DYNAMIC_CHECK when the API intentionally relies on runtime propagation rules, and CX_NO_CHECK for failures that should propagate implicitly. I catch where I can recover or translate meaningfully. When wrapping a dependency failure, I preserve its original exception through PREVIOUS.

Example
A repository failure might become an application-specific document-read exception while retaining the technical cause. I do not add an empty CATCH merely to satisfy a signature, and I do not replace an established framework error contract without considering its caller.

Avoid
NO_CHECK does not mean an exception cannot be caught; DYNAMIC_CHECK does not mean it can cross any procedure interface without declaration.

column1: ABAP-11 | Which modern ABAP expressions are useful, and when should you avoid them?
column2:
Short answer
Inline declarations, VALUE, CORRESPONDING, COND, CONV, and string templates can make intent clearer and reduce temporary variables. I use them when the supported release and language version allow them. A deeply nested expression that hides branching or expensive work is harder to debug, so I prefer named intermediate steps when they explain the business logic.

Example
CORRESPONDING maps components by name unless explicit mapping changes that behavior. CONV converts a value; it does not validate every business rule. A short expression for selecting a default is useful, while a dense REDUCE replacing several unrelated calculations may be less readable.

Avoid
Modern expression syntax is not synonymous with ABAP SQL and does not automatically improve runtime performance.

column1: ABAP-12 | How do you handle amounts, quantities, dates, and timestamps correctly?
column2:
Short answer
I keep amounts with currency and quantities with their unit, using suitable decimal types and the application's conversion rules. I distinguish a date from a timestamp and preserve time-zone context when converting instants for users. Formatting is a presentation concern; calculations and interfaces need stable semantics, precision, and documented rounding behavior.

Example
Adding 100 EUR to 100 USD without conversion produces a meaningless total. A deadline stored as an instant can cross a local date boundary for another user. Test currency decimal differences, daylight-saving transitions, and rounding at the intended business boundary.

Avoid
A numeric field alone does not explain its currency or unit, and a local date-time string is not an unambiguous global instant.
JSON and XML: values and mapping

These are two explicitly designed representations of the same sample values, not a universal automatic JSON/XML conversion.

column1: ABAP-13 | When would you use RTTI, RTTC, or dynamic ABAP?
column2:
Short answer
RTTI inspects runtime type information; RTTC creates type descriptions used to construct data objects dynamically. They are valuable for generic frameworks whose structure is genuinely unknown beforehand. For normal business logic I prefer static types, because they make contracts, navigation, checks, and maintenance easier. Dynamic names and selections also require explicit validation.

Example
A configurable export framework may need to inspect component metadata and construct a selected output shape. An ordinary invoice service with a stable schema normally does not. Validate allowed fields rather than turning arbitrary user text into dynamic SQL fragments.

Avoid
Dynamic programming is not inherently more reusable, and escaping values alone does not validate arbitrary dynamic SQL identifiers or syntax.
