column1: ABAP-14 | How would you investigate an ABAP failure without changing production behavior?
column2:
Short answer
I start with the exact operation, inputs, time, user, and system context, then correlate application logs, error details, and a dump if one exists. I reproduce with controlled data and inspect the failing call path. A fix should address the cause and preserve authorization, locking, and transaction boundaries, with a focused regression scenario.

Example
In classic systems ST22 can identify a dump and its call stack; debugging or tracing must use appropriate permissions and scope. A background or update failure may run under a different user and execution context from the original dialog request.

Avoid
Suppressing an exception or granting broad authorization may hide the symptom while leaving the defect and data-integrity risk intact.

column1: BASE-01 | What changes when a method receives a CHANGING parameter by value instead of by reference?
column2:
Short answer
By reference, the formal parameter aliases the caller's data, so allowed writes affect it immediately. With VALUE, a local value is changed and copied back on normal completion. An exception leaving the method prevents that normal copy-back. This difference affects error guarantees, but it does not undo database writes or changes made through referenced objects.

Example
Suppose a method changes a plain integer from 10 to 20 and then raises a class-based exception. A reference CHANGING parameter can leave 20 visible to the caller; a value-result parameter retains the caller's 10. Test both failure and success paths before changing an established signature.

Avoid
Pass-by-value is not a transaction rollback and does not clone objects behind reference parameters.
Parameter values after exceptional exit

Compare the same assignment under two transfer modes. The final caller value is visible evidence of the difference.
Explain it: Which result changes if the method returns normally? What changes if the parameter holds an object reference?
Limit: This assumes a plain integer, value-result passing, and no additional side effects.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • How would this change with an object reference parameter?
  • Can an IMPORTING reference variable still expose a mutable object?
Strong answer criteria
  • Separates parameter direction from transfer mode
  • Explains exceptional copy-back behavior
  • Identifies external side effects
Verification evidence
A small method-call test showing caller values after normal return and exception.

Read and verify
  • SAP: Pass by value
    Formal parameters are local copies; parameter direction controls transfer.

column1: BASE-02 | A copied structure contains a string, a nested table, and an object reference. Is it an independent snapshot?
column2:
Short answer
The string and nested table are value components: changing their copied contents does not intentionally mutate the source value. The reference component is different: copying it preserves a reference to the same object. Mutating that object's state through either structure is observable through the other. A true snapshot therefore needs an explicit policy for references and mutable reachable objects.

Example
For an approval snapshot, copying ls_request preserves the item values but does not freeze an attached mutable pricing object. Store the calculated price as a value, use an immutable collaborator, or implement deliberate cloning with defined identity and cycle handling. Internal sharing optimizations do not change these language-level semantics.

Avoid
A deep ABAP type is not a promise that ordinary assignment recursively clones the entire object graph.
Value components versus a shared referent

Two structure values own independent string values but lead to the same pricing object. The arrow targets explain why a getter can expose mutable state.
Explain it: Which change affects only ls_copy, and which change affects an object visible through both?
Limit: Conceptual object identity, not physical memory addresses or a particular sharing optimization.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • Which components need copying for an audit snapshot?
  • How would you test sharing without inspecting memory addresses?
Strong answer criteria
  • Distinguishes value components from references
  • Preserves object identity semantics
  • Defines snapshot ownership
Verification evidence
Mutation tests for a copied string, nested row, and referenced object's attribute.

Read and verify
  • SAP: Sharing between dynamic data objects
    Distinguishes copying reference values from internal sharing of strings and tables.

column1: BASE-03 | A large temporary internal table is no longer needed. When would you choose CLEAR or FREE?
column2:
Short answer
For a headerless internal table, both remove its rows. CLEAR keeps the initial memory requirement available, while FREE also releases that initial allocation. I use CLEAR when the same table will soon be populated again and FREE when retaining its allocation has no useful purpose. Neither deletes the declared variable or guarantees an immediate reduction in operating-system memory.

Example
In a package loop, repeatedly freeing and rebuilding a modest buffer may add allocation work. After a one-off large reconciliation, releasing the unused table can reduce retained application memory. Measure used and allocated memory in the relevant session before drawing conclusions from process memory alone.

Avoid
Do not claim CLEAR retains every byte ever allocated, or that FREE destroys referenced objects still reachable elsewhere.
Three distinct state and memory lifetimes

Empty row slots and the initial allocation are deliberately drawn separately. A new object does not imply a new internal session or empty class cache.
Explain it: Why can recreating a service leave a test-order failure unchanged?
Limit: Allocation diagram is qualitative; measure actual ABAP memory and cache lifetime in the target context.

Read and verify
  • SAP: CLEAR
    CLEAR releases table rows but retains the initial memory requirement; FREE releases that too.

column1: BASE-04 | A dynamic ASSIGN fails, but IS ASSIGNED is still true. How can the program update the wrong field?
column2:
Short answer
A failed dynamic assignment can leave the field symbol pointing at its previous target. IS ASSIGNED then says only that some assignment exists, not that the latest lookup succeeded. I check the statement's result immediately and avoid using the alias after failure. On a supporting release, ELSE UNASSIGN makes the failure state explicit; otherwise I unassign before attempting the lookup.

Example
A mapper assigns component PRICE successfully, then requests nonexistent component PRCIE. If it tests only IS ASSIGNED, a subsequent write may overwrite PRICE. A regression test must include a successful lookup followed by an invalid one using the same field symbol.

Avoid
An assigned field symbol is not evidence that the most recent dynamic ASSIGN succeeded.
Stale aliases and overwritten return codes

The first sequence can write to the previous target. The second takes a success branch for a different operation than the programmer intended.
Explain it: Which test requires a successful operation before the failure to expose the defect?
Limit: Only statements documented to set sy-subrc replace it. Assignment failure behavior depends on the exact form and additions.

Read and verify
  • SAP: ASSIGN, ELSE UNASSIGN
    Failed assignments may preserve an earlier alias unless explicitly unassigned.

column1: BASE-05 | A READ TABLE fails, yet a later IF sy-subrc = 0 takes the success branch. What do you inspect?
column2:
Short answer
I inspect every intervening statement that can set sy-subrc. It is a shared runtime field, not a result permanently attached to READ TABLE. I branch immediately or preserve the result in a named local variable before further work. For modern expressions, I use their documented exception or predicate behavior instead of assuming they set sy-subrc like classic statements.

Example
A failed lookup is followed by a successful FIND used to prepare logging text. Testing sy-subrc afterward now tests FIND. Include a missing-record case with successful logging preparation; merely testing an immediate lookup in isolation would miss the actual sequence.

Avoid
Not every statement resets sy-subrc, and a table expression is not a drop-in sy-subrc-producing READ TABLE.

The first sequence can write to the previous target. The second takes a success branch for a different operation than the programmer intended.
Explain it: Which test requires a successful operation before the failure to expose the defect?
Limit: Only statements documented to set sy-subrc replace it. Assignment failure behavior depends on the exact form and additions.

Read and verify

    Return values belong to particular statements and can be replaced by later statements.

column1: BASE-06 | An import must reject precision loss rather than silently round or truncate. Where does EXACT help?
column2:
Short answer
EXACT requests a lossless assignment or calculation and raises an appropriate exception when the requested result cannot be represented without loss. CONV applies ordinary conversion rules and is not equivalent validation. I place the check at a typed boundary, translate conversion failures into useful input feedback, and still validate domain rules such as permitted signs, identifiers, and currency.

Example
Converting a runtime text longer than a fixed character target can otherwise discard characters. For a two-decimal packed result, EXACT can reject a calculation such as one divided by three. That is useful when rounding is forbidden; when rounding is required, make the business rounding step explicit instead.

Avoid
EXACT does not prove that a technically representable value is an allowed business value.
Conversion, rounding, and reduction counterexamples

A lost character, a one-cent difference, and a false maximum reveal three unrelated errors that concise syntax can hide.
Explain it: Which expected results change with a different rounding mode, and which are independent of rounding?
Limit: Half-up and two decimals are explicit exercise assumptions, not a universal currency rule. MAX notation is explanatory.

Read and verify

    Official executable illustrations of lossless assignments and calculations.

column1: BASE-07 | Two invoice totals differ by one cent although both use decimal types. How do you diagnose rounding?
column2:
Short answer
I compare the sequence of calculations, intermediate precision, and the prescribed rounding point and mode. Rounding every line and then summing can differ from summing precise values and rounding once. Currency metadata does not automatically make an arbitrary calculation compliant. I retain currency context, use appropriate decimal types, and encode the agreed rule explicitly with boundary tests.

Example
Under an agreed half-up, two-decimal rule, two positive line results of 0.005 become 0.01 each if rounded separately, totaling 0.02. Their unrounded sum is 0.010 and rounds to 0.01. The correct amount depends on the specified line-versus-document rule.

Avoid
Choosing decfloat34 or formatting two decimals does not settle the business rounding policy.
Conversion, rounding, and reduction counterexamples

A lost character, a one-cent difference, and a false maximum reveal three unrelated errors that concise syntax can hide.
Explain it: Which expected results change with a different rounding mode, and which are independent of rounding?
Limit: Half-up and two decimals are explicit exercise assumptions, not a universal currency rule. MAX notation is explanatory.

Interviewer follow-ups

  • Where is currency conversion applied relative to tax rounding?
Strong answer criteria
  • Traces intermediate precision
  • Names rounding stage and mode
  • Keeps currency semantics
Verification evidence
Worked positive/negative boundary examples with independently calculated expected totals.

Read and verify

    Decimal places, precision, and explicit rounding modes are distinct choices.

column1: BASE-08 | Why can replacing MOVE-CORRESPONDING with CORRESPONDING erase an existing structure field?
column2:
Short answer
An ordinary CORRESPONDING constructor creates a new result, so target components absent from the source become initial. MOVE-CORRESPONDING between structures leaves unmatched target components unchanged. BASE can supply starting values for a constructor result before matching components overwrite them. I specify the desired merge contract rather than assuming all name-based assignments preserve existing state.

Example
ls_existing contains status Approved and a note. The source contains only a new note: plain CORRESPONDING clears the unmatched status; BASE preserves it. But if the source type contains status with an initial value, that matching component still overwrites the base. Field presence requires a separate update contract.

Avoid
BASE preserves unmatched components; it does not mean ignore every initial source value or implement PATCH automatically.
Three mapping cases and two presence cases

The matching initial status overwrites BASE just as a populated status does. A separate parameter table shows why zero cannot encode omission.
Explain it: Which source needs a presence flag when the source type always contains status?
Limit: Structure mapping example; internal-table BASE preserves rows under different construction semantics.

Read and verify

    Compares MOVE-CORRESPONDING with CORRESPONDING and BASE.

column1: BASE-09 | Unsorted orders must be processed once per customer with their member rows. How does GROUP BY change the loop?
column2:
Short answer
LOOP AT with GROUP BY first forms groups and then executes the group loop. Equal group keys are collected even if rows are not adjacent, unlike traditional control-level processing that relies on ordering. I choose explicit group-key binding when it improves clarity and use LOOP AT GROUP for members. Group order and member order still need a deliberate contract.

Example
Input customers A, B, A creates two groups, with both A orders together. The group body executes twice, not once per order. WITHOUT MEMBERS is suitable when only group keys are needed, but then a later member loop is not available.

Avoid
Grouping an internal table is not database aggregation, and its default group order is not automatically business sort order.
Unsorted group membership and explicit filter keys

Arrows bring nonadjacent A rows into one group. The grouping total is computed from members, not read from the representative row.
Explain it: What changes with WITHOUT MEMBERS, and why is an arbitrary OR predicate not automatically a basic FILTER condition?
Limit: Source rows and totals are illustrative; no measured performance advantage is asserted.

Read and verify
  • SAP: LOOP AT itab, GROUP BY
    Grouping and group iteration are separate phases; prior sorting is not required.

column1: BASE-10 | A FILTER expression is proposed for a standard table with an empty primary key. Is that enough?
column2:
Short answer
For the basic FILTER form, access must use a suitable sorted or hashed key. A standard table can work when it has an appropriate secondary key selected with USING KEY; an empty primary key alone is insufficient. I also check that the predicate meets the selected key's rules. A FOR expression or a clear loop may fit an arbitrary predicate better.

Example
A standard table retains arrival order but has a sorted secondary key by customer. FILTER USING KEY can select that customer. A complex OR predicate over unrelated columns should not be forced into a key-based FILTER shape or justified by an unmeasured speed claim.

Avoid
FILTER is not a general-purpose synonym for every WHERE expression supported by LOOP or FOR.
Unsorted group membership and explicit filter keys

Arrows bring nonadjacent A rows into one group. The grouping total is computed from members, not read from the representative row.
Explain it: What changes with WITHOUT MEMBERS, and why is an arbitrary OR predicate not automatically a basic FILTER condition?
Limit: Source rows and totals are illustrative; no measured performance advantage is asserted.

    Defines sorted/hash key requirements and supported predicate forms.

column1: BASE-11 | A REDUCE expression calculates a maximum, but all-negative input returns zero. What went wrong?
column2:
Short answer
The accumulator's initial value is part of the algorithm. Starting a maximum at zero invents a candidate that may not exist in an all-negative input set. I define empty-input semantics and initialize from a valid first member or represent the absence of a result explicitly. I also choose accumulator types deliberately so intermediate overflow or rounding cannot hide behind concise syntax.

Example
For values -8 and -3, a zero-initialized maximum remains zero although the correct maximum is -3. Empty input may require no result or a domain exception, not the same number. The expression should remain readable enough that reviewers can identify initialization, iteration, and state update.

Avoid
REDUCE does not supply mathematically correct initial values or empty-set semantics on the developer's behalf.
Conversion, rounding, and reduction counterexamples

A lost character, a one-cent difference, and a false maximum reveal three unrelated errors that concise syntax can hide.
Explain it: Which expected results change with a different rounding mode, and which are independent of rounding?
Limit: Half-up and two decimals are explicit exercise assumptions, not a universal currency rule. MAX notation is explanatory.

Read and verify

    Shows explicit initialization and iterative accumulator updates.

column1: BASE-12 | A report accepts a filter value and a sort-column name. Is escaping quotes sufficient for safe SQL?
column2:
Short answer
No. Data values and SQL identifiers are different inputs. I bind values through host variables in static ABAP SQL where possible. For configurable identifiers or dynamic clauses, I restrict them to a server-controlled allowlist and validate the supported syntax. Escaping a string value cannot authorize a table name, column name, operator, or an entire user-supplied WHERE fragment.

Example
A search value containing an apostrophe should remain a value. A sort request is mapped from an accepted business option to a known column; arbitrary SQL text is rejected. Authorization predicates are built independently and cannot be removed by user filter or ordering choices.

Avoid
Input that is safely quoted as a literal is not therefore safe as SQL syntax or an authorized data access.
Two input kinds and two safe handling paths

The apostrophe is intentionally harmless data on the left. The sort request on the right selects a predefined identifier rather than supplying executable SQL.
Explain it: Why would quoting the sort option as a literal fail to solve identifier validation?
Limit: Conceptual SQL boundary; available dynamic-programming helpers and API release status depend on the target environment.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • How would you test an input that is valid syntax but unauthorized?
  • Which parts of the SQL shape can remain completely static?
Strong answer criteria
  • Separates values and identifiers
  • Uses explicit allowed SQL shapes
  • Preserves authorization predicates
Verification evidence
Negative tests for quoted values, forbidden columns, injected operators, and unauthorized records.

Read and verify
  • SAP: Prevent SQL injection
    Prefer static SQL; validate and escape dynamic content using supported facilities.

column1: BASE-13 | A resource release is placed only in CLEANUP. Why can it remain unreleased after success?
column2:
Short answer
ABAP CLEANUP is part of exception unwinding, not a finally block that runs after every TRY. It runs for the relevant protected context when an exception propagates to an outer handler; it is not the normal-success path. I arrange explicit release on successful completion and on relevant exceptional exits, while respecting the actual owner's lock or resource lifetime.

Example
An application-owned temporary handle is opened, processing succeeds, and ENDTRY is reached: CLEANUP alone does not close it. Test success, an exception caught locally, and one propagated outward. Cleanup failures also need handling so they do not obscure the original failure or escape a CLEANUP block.

Avoid
Do not assume CLEANUP automatically runs after a CATCH in the same TRY, or release framework-owned locks prematurely.
Exceptional exits and preserved causes

The table names three exit paths that require separate reasoning. The exception chain carries the lower-level diagnosis through a meaningful service-level failure.
Explain it: Which path would a test of only propagated exceptions miss?
Limit: Simplified non-resumable scenarios; exact nesting and handlers determine CLEANUP execution. Resource ownership remains application-specific.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • What changes when the exception is caught inside the same TRY?
  • Who owns release when a caller supplied the resource?
Strong answer criteria
  • Distinguishes CLEANUP from finally
  • Covers normal and exceptional paths
  • Respects ownership
Verification evidence
Instrumented resource tests show one correct release on every intended exit.

Read and verify
  • SAP: Exception system response
    Explains stack unwinding and when CLEANUP blocks run or do not run.

column1: BASE-14 | An optional limit parameter is omitted in one call and explicitly set to zero in another. How can a method distinguish them?
column2:
Short answer
IS SUPPLIED tests whether an actual parameter was provided, independently of its value. IS INITIAL tests the value and cannot distinguish an omitted zero-defaulted argument from an explicit zero. I use presence only when the API deliberately assigns different meaning to omission. If a wrapper always forwards a parameter, it must preserve the intended presence contract explicitly.

Example
For a pagination helper, omission may mean use the configured limit, while zero may mean return no rows. A wrapper that forwards its own initial variable makes the downstream parameter supplied. Test the direct calls and the wrapper path, rather than silently changing zero into the default.

Avoid
OPTIONAL does not automatically preserve absent-versus-present semantics across another method boundary.
Three mapping cases and two presence cases

The matching initial status overwrites BASE just as a populated status does. A separate parameter table shows why zero cannot encode omission.
Explain it: Which source needs a presence flag when the source type always contains status?
Limit: Structure mapping example; internal-table BASE preserves rows under different construction semantics.

Read and verify
  • SAP: IS SUPPLIED
    Presence of an actual argument is independent of its initial value.

column1: BASE-15 | A single-line INSERT INTO TABLE hits an existing unique primary key. Does it update the existing row?
column2:
Short answer
No. For this internal-table insertion case, the new line is not inserted and sy-subrc indicates the duplicate. The existing row is not an implicit update target. I decide whether the operation means reject, merge, or replace, then implement that policy explicitly. I do not generalize this return-code behavior to every constructor, secondary-key conflict, or database insertion form.

Example
An import contains order 7 twice with different amounts. A unique hashed table prevents duplicate keys, but silently ignoring the second line can conceal inconsistent source data. Compare payloads if duplicates are allowed only when identical; otherwise report both the key and conflicting input position.

Avoid
Uniqueness enforcement is not a complete deduplication policy, and INSERT is not an automatic upsert.
Duplicate insertion and empty authorization boundaries

A duplicate unique key preserves the original row for the specified insertion form. An initial selection range has a very different meaning from an empty list of permissions.
Explain it: How would you distinguish identical duplicates from conflicting ones, and prove a user with no plants sees nothing?
Limit: Single-line INSERT INTO TABLE with a unique primary key; other insertion and key-conflict forms need their own documented handling.

Read and verify

    Single-line insertion with duplicate unique primary key returns sy-subrc 4.

column1: BASE-16 | An authorization helper returns an empty range table. Why is WHERE field IN range unsafe as the only access restriction?
column2:
Short answer
An initial selection range represents no restriction for IN, so it must not be used to encode 'the user may see nothing.' I define empty authorization results separately and return no rows or reject the operation before querying. Nonempty ranges combine inclusion and exclusion rules; their semantics differ from a plain list whose empty membership set would match nothing.

Example
If a user has no permitted plants, the application must not execute an otherwise unrestricted read with an empty plant range. Keep optional user filters separate from mandatory authorization constraints. Test no permissions as well as one permitted plant and exclusions.

Avoid
An empty ABAP selection range is not the same as an SQL list containing zero allowed values.
Duplicate insertion and empty authorization boundaries

A duplicate unique key preserves the original row for the specified insertion form. An initial selection range has a very different meaning from an empty list of permissions.
Explain it: How would you distinguish identical duplicates from conflicting ones, and prove a user with no plants sees nothing?
Limit: Single-line INSERT INTO TABLE with a unique primary key; other insertion and key-conflict forms need their own documented handling.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • How do you distinguish an optional filter from mandatory authorization?
  • What result do you expect from a range containing only exclusions?
Strong answer criteria
  • Recognizes initial-range semantics
  • Fails closed for no permissions
  • Separates user filtering from security
Verification evidence
A denied-user test proves zero data and zero aggregate leakage with an empty authorization result.

    Defines inclusion/exclusion semantics and the initial selection-table case.

column1: OO-01 | Explain abstraction, encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism with one example.
column2:
Short answer
For a delivery service, abstraction exposes a send operation while hiding transport details. Encapsulation protects its internal state and invariants. Inheritance can specialize a genuine base contract. Polymorphism lets the caller invoke send through an interface while different implementations deliver by different channels. These ideas help changes stay local to the responsible component.

Example
A notification coordinator can receive an email sender or a test sender through the same interface. The coordinator should not inspect the concrete class to decide how to send; doing that would weaken the polymorphic design.

Avoid
Encapsulation means protecting valid behavior and state, not merely generating getters and setters for every attribute.
OO interfaces and dependency injection

The service depends on a repository contract. Production and test implementations fit the same socket; the composition boundary supplies the appropriate collaborator.
Explain it: Which object chooses the implementation, and what does a double-based test fail to prove?
Limit: The plug is a design metaphor, not a SAP connector or code signature. Injection does not itself guarantee a good abstraction or production integration.

column1: OO-02 | What can an ABAP interface contain, and when would you use one?
column2:
Short answer
An ABAP interface defines a contract implemented by classes. It can declare methods and other components such as types, constants, attributes, and events; it is not limited to abstract methods. I normally keep behavioral interfaces narrow so callers depend on the capability they need and tests can supply a substitute implementation.

Example
A price-provider interface can expose a calculation operation without publishing database access. Two implementations need not be similar classes overall; sharing the required business contract is enough. Ordinary interfaces and specialized BAdI interfaces have different restrictions.

Avoid
An interface is not an abstract class, and a collection of similarly named methods alone does not establish a meaningful common contract.

column1: OO-03 | How do ABSTRACT and FINAL affect classes and methods?
column2:
Short answer
An abstract class cannot be instantiated directly and may provide shared implementation. It does not have to contain an abstract method. An abstract method has no implementation there and must be implemented before a concrete subclass can be instantiated. FINAL prevents further subclassing for a class, or further redefinition for a method.

Example
An abstract document processor could implement logging while requiring a concrete processing step. If no supported specialization is intended, a final class communicates that choice. Marking a class final does not stop it implementing interfaces or receiving collaborators.

Avoid
Do not import another language's virtual keyword or method-overloading rules into ABAP; use ABAP's actual redefinition and signature rules.

column1: OO-04 | How do upcasting and downcasting work in ABAP Objects?
column2:
Short answer
Upcasting views an object through a compatible superclass or interface reference and preserves the same object. Downcasting requests a more specific compatible type and can fail at runtime if the actual object does not support it. I use a type check or handle CX_SY_MOVE_CAST_ERROR when a downcast is genuinely necessary.

Example
A reference typed to a payment interface can point to a card implementation. Converting it back to the card type does not create a new card object. Frequent downcasts often indicate the interface is missing a required capability or the caller knows too much.

Avoid
Casting a reference changes the accessible static view, not the object's dynamic type or stored data.

column1: OO-05 | What is the difference between instance and static methods and constructors?
column2:
Short answer
An instance method acts on an object and can access its instance state. A static method belongs to the class and has no implicit current instance. The instance constructor initializes a newly created object. The class constructor initializes class-level state when the runtime first requires it in the internal session; I avoid unpredictable heavy work there.

Example
A class can contain static and instance methods together. Restricting creation or declaring a class abstract affects instantiation; merely adding CLASS-METHODS does not. Constructor injection makes mandatory dependencies visible before business methods are called.

Avoid
ABAP does not make a class uninstantiable simply because it has static methods, and class data is not automatically shared system-wide.

    Compare the language contract with the Clean ABAP design guidance. Project conventions can differ from style recommendations.

column1: OO-06 | When do you prefer composition over inheritance?
column2:
Short answer
I prefer composition when behavior varies independently or I want to replace a dependency without coupling classes to a hierarchy. Inheritance is appropriate when the subclass really preserves the base contract and specialization is intentional. Composition makes ownership and collaboration explicit and avoids a deep hierarchy used only to share a few helper methods.

Example
A report service can contain a repository, an authorization policy, and a formatter. Different implementations can be supplied independently. Making every report inherit from a large superclass may entangle unrelated persistence, output, and authorization decisions.

Avoid
Code reuse alone is weak justification for inheritance; a subclass that violates caller expectations is not a sound substitute.

column1: OO-07 | How do dependency injection and dependency inversion differ?
column2:
Short answer
Dependency inversion is a design principle: business policy should depend on suitable abstractions rather than concrete infrastructure details. Dependency injection is a way to supply a collaborator from outside, commonly through a constructor. Together they make dependencies visible and replaceable, but injection alone does not guarantee a useful abstraction or a good responsibility split.

Example
An approval service receives a repository interface. Production composition supplies a database implementation; an ABAP Unit test supplies a controlled double. The service should not immediately instantiate its own concrete repository and ignore the injected dependency.

Avoid
Injecting a concrete class everywhere may aid construction while still leaving the business layer tightly coupled to infrastructure.

The service depends on a repository contract. Production and test implementations fit the same socket; the composition boundary supplies the appropriate collaborator.

column1: OO-08 | How would you apply SOLID without overengineering?
column2:
Short answer
I use SOLID as questions about change. Does each component have a coherent responsibility? Can variation be added without repeatedly editing central logic? Do substitutes preserve expectations? Are interfaces small enough for their clients? Do business rules depend on abstractions? I introduce structure to solve an observed need, not to maximize the number of classes.

Example
Separating tax calculation from database retrieval can support focused tests and independent changes. Creating an interface for a tiny stable helper with no substitution need may add little value. Discuss one concrete change scenario rather than reciting five slogans.

Avoid
Single responsibility does not mean one method per class, and open/closed does not mean existing code must never be changed.

column1: OO-09 | When are Strategy and Factory useful?
column2:
Short answer
Strategy packages interchangeable behavior behind a common contract, such as choosing a pricing rule. A factory centralizes construction when callers should not know concrete classes or setup details. They often work together: configuration selects a strategy that a factory creates. A simple static creation helper is not automatically the inheritance-based Factory Method pattern.

Example
For domestic and export pricing, the coordinator receives a pricing strategy. The composition boundary decides which implementation is appropriate. If only one simple construction path exists, direct construction outside the business logic may be clearer than an elaborate factory hierarchy.

Avoid
Do not call every method that returns an object Factory Method without distinguishing a simple factory from the formal pattern.

column1: OO-10 | What do Adapter and Facade solve in SAP integration code?
column2:
Short answer
An adapter translates one contract into another, allowing a client to use an existing service through its preferred interface. A facade offers a simpler operation over a subsystem with several steps. For a legacy posting API, either pattern can isolate mapping and error translation while keeping its transaction, authorization, and release limitations visible.

Example
A posting facade might coordinate validation and mapping; an adapter can translate an application's request into a legacy function module's structures. The caller still needs to know whether persistence is synchronous and who owns commit and rollback.

Avoid
Wrapping an unreleased SAP object does not by itself make that underlying dependency released, cloud compliant, or clean-core Level A.

column1: OO-11 | What are the limitations of Singleton in ABAP?
column2:
Short answer
A conventional singleton restricts construction and returns a stored instance through a class-level accessor. Its scope is normally the ABAP internal session, not the whole SAP landscape. It can introduce hidden dependencies, persistent mutable test state, and difficult substitution. I use it only when that lifetime and access model are deliberate requirements.

Example
A configuration cache might need invalidation when customizing changes. A singleton that retains yesterday's assumptions or leaks state between tests becomes a correctness problem. Often an explicitly constructed shared service with an injected interface gives clearer ownership.

Avoid
A singleton does not synchronize business updates across sessions, work processes, application servers, or users.

column1: OO-12 | How do ABAP OO events differ from durable business events?
column2:
Short answer
An ABAP OO event notifies registered handlers in the current runtime context and can decouple a publisher from listeners. A durable business event used for workflow or external integration needs a separate delivery mechanism, transaction coordination, monitoring, and retry design. Similar terminology does not mean a local event provides durable asynchronous messaging.

Example
An ALV interaction can raise an event handled by a controller registered with SET HANDLER. Starting an external approval process after a document save requires the supported business-event or integration mechanism, including handling duplicates and failures.

Avoid
RAISE EVENT by itself does not persist a message or guarantee workflow creation after a commit.
Duplicate events and stale approvals

The event identity and current business state decide whether to apply, ignore or reject the request.
Explain it: Two consumers process the same event simultaneously: what prevents a double effect?
Limit: Exact transactional deduplication mechanisms depend on the chosen infrastructure.

column1: OO-13 | What would you change first in a difficult legacy ABAP method?
column2:
Short answer
I first identify its observable behavior, callers, and transaction responsibilities. Then I make small, reviewable improvements such as naming unclear concepts, separating a calculation from I/O, and removing repeated logic. I add focused tests around risky behavior before larger restructuring. Preserving the established contract matters more than turning every statement into modern syntax.

Example
A safe extraction might isolate discount calculation while keeping posting and commit behavior unchanged. In this project, new tables use lt_, structures ls_, and constants co_; these are team preferences, not mandatory ABAP syntax or universal Clean ABAP rules.

Avoid
A broad stylistic rewrite without behavior evidence can introduce regressions and make review harder, even if the result looks more modern.

column1: OO-14 | How do you make an OO design testable, and what should ABAP Unit assert?
column2:
Short answer
I separate business decisions from database, clock, authorization, and external-service access through appropriate seams. Tests exercise observable behavior with controlled inputs and meaningful assertions. I cover boundaries, failures, and interactions that matter to the contract. Coverage helps identify untested areas, but it does not prove that assertions are correct or that real integration works.

Example
For an approval policy, test below, at, and above a threshold, plus a missing approver. A repository double can simulate not-found and technical failure. Separate integration checks must verify the real persistence and authorization behavior in the target system.

Avoid
A test that only asserts that a method returned, or mirrors its implementation step by step, provides weak evidence.

The service depends on a repository contract. Production and test implementations fit the same socket; the composition boundary supplies the appropriate collaborator.
Explain it: Which object chooses the implementation, and what does a double-based test fail to prove?

The widening base suggests many focused checks, but there is no mandatory numerical ratio.

column1: OO-15 | How does MVC separate responsibilities?
column2:
Short answer
The Model represents application data and relevant behavior. The View presents information and collects interaction. The Controller interprets user interaction and coordinates model and view changes. Frameworks implement the pattern differently; MVC is a responsibility split, not a fixed network sequence that every application follows.

Example
In SAPUI5, a controller can handle a button press while a bound model supplies view data. Backend business rules still belong in the appropriate service or BO, not only in the browser controller.

Avoid
MVC does not mean copying all backend business logic into the UI controller or assuming the view must always be manually rebuilt.

column1: OODEEP-01 | A method named reserve returns a reservation ID. Which promises must be explicit beyond its parameter types?
column2:
Short answer
I define accepted inputs, the observable success result, allowed state changes, and failure behavior. The caller needs to know whether the reservation is merely buffered or durable, whether repetition is safe, and who owns transaction completion. Those promises belong in the contract and its tests. A matching signature alone cannot tell another developer whether combining two operations is safe.

Example
One implementation returns an ID before save; another commits immediately. Both compile against the same interface but are not interchangeable for a caller that reserves two items atomically. Document the intended boundary in ABAP Doc and test failure of the second item against the first one's state.

Avoid
RETURNING an identifier does not itself promise committed persistence, and a method name cannot replace a transaction contract.
A concrete counterexample to substitutability

A valid quantity-one call exposes a behavioral violation invisible in matching parameter types. The lower table separates redefinition from a genuinely new capability.
Explain it: Would downcasting every caller to Provider B repair the contract? What else besides accepted inputs must agree?
Limit: Hypothetical contract; a narrower published domain would lead to a different assessment. No executable interface is implied.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • What state is allowed after reserve raises an exception?
  • What is the result when the same business request is retried?
Strong answer criteria
  • Defines success and failure state
  • States transaction ownership
  • Defines repeat-call semantics
Verification evidence
Contract tests plus documentation covering buffered success, persistence boundary, and repeated requests.

column1: OODEEP-02 | A new price-provider implementation rejects quantities below ten although the interface accepts any positive quantity. Is it a valid substitute?
column2:
Short answer
No, if the published contract accepts every positive quantity, the new provider strengthens the precondition and breaks callers that validly request one unit. I either preserve the shared contract, expose the narrower capability separately, or change the contract through a managed migration. I compare outputs, errors, and side effects as well as input types when assessing substitutability.

Example
A checkout calls the provider through an interface with quantity one and expects a quote. A subclass or implementation that raises an unsupported-quantity error for that valid input violates the agreed behavior even though activation succeeds. Run the same contract scenarios against each implementation.

Avoid
Implementing an interface or passing a cast check proves type compatibility, not behavioral substitutability.
A concrete counterexample to substitutability

A valid quantity-one call exposes a behavioral violation invisible in matching parameter types. The lower table separates redefinition from a genuinely new capability.
Explain it: Would downcasting every caller to Provider B repair the contract? What else besides accepted inputs must agree?
Limit: Hypothetical contract; a narrower published domain would lead to a different assessment. No executable interface is implied.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • Can a substitute silently return a different currency?
  • Which common tests would run against every provider?
Strong answer criteria
  • Identifies strengthened precondition
  • Checks postconditions and side effects
  • Uses shared behavioral tests
Verification evidence
A contract suite exercises minimum positive quantity, currency, failures, and repeat calls for both providers.

    Interface references provide the common call surface for different implementations.

column1: OODEEP-03 | Two unrelated services share a capability and some validation code. Should their callers depend on an abstract superclass?
column2:
Short answer
I separate the public capability from implementation reuse. An interface can express the capability without imposing a class hierarchy. Shared validation can be a collaborator. An abstract base class is justified when there is a stable specialization relationship and a useful shared lifecycle or template, not simply similar code. I also consider that a class has only one superclass.

Example
A document exporter and a notification sender may both support cancellation but have unrelated lifecycles. A narrow cancellation interface lets a coordinator address either, while shared policy is composed where needed. For a genuine family of parsers with enforced shared steps, an abstract template may be appropriate.

Avoid
An abstract superclass is not automatically a better contract because it can carry reusable implementation.
A concrete counterexample to substitutability

A valid quantity-one call exposes a behavioral violation invisible in matching parameter types. The lower table separates redefinition from a genuinely new capability.
Explain it: Would downcasting every caller to Provider B repair the contract? What else besides accepted inputs must agree?
Limit: Hypothetical contract; a narrower published domain would lead to a different assessment. No executable interface is implied.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • Which invariant would the superclass enforce?
  • How would the design accommodate a class already inheriting from a framework base?
Strong answer criteria
  • Separates contract from reuse
  • Tests the is-a relationship
  • Accounts for independent variation
Verification evidence
A responsibility sketch shows the caller's minimal interface and the owner of shared validation.

column1: OODEEP-04 | A subclass needs a different implementation and an extra mandatory input for an inherited method. Can REDEFINITION add it?
column2:
Short answer
No. Redefinition replaces an eligible inherited instance method's implementation while preserving its interface. ABAP does not use same-name, different-signature method overloading to solve this. If the additional input changes the operation's contract, I introduce a distinct operation or a deliberate compatible contract evolution. The existing inherited operation must still satisfy callers using the base type.

Example
A base method formats a document. A specialized format requires an extra profile: provide a separately named operation, or configure a validated collaborator before use if that fits the existing contract. Requiring callers to downcast merely to make the inherited method usable exposes a broken abstraction.

Avoid
Redefinition is not method overloading, and optional parameters do not automatically make every behavioral change compatible.
A concrete counterexample to substitutability

A valid quantity-one call exposes a behavioral violation invisible in matching parameter types. The lower table separates redefinition from a genuinely new capability.
Explain it: Would downcasting every caller to Provider B repair the contract? What else besides accepted inputs must agree?
Limit: Hypothetical contract; a narrower published domain would lead to a different assessment. No executable interface is implied.

column1: OODEEP-05 | A local test class needs access to private state. What does granting friendship expose, and what does it not imply?
column2:
Short answer
Friendship grants access to the granting class's protected and private components. It is unilateral, so the reverse access is not automatic. A friend of a superclass is not automatically a friend of its subclasses; subclasses of a friend can also gain access. I keep the grant narrow and first ask whether the test can assert the public behavior instead.

Example
A focused final local test class may need a legacy injection seam. Making every production attribute public is broader than necessary. Granting friendship to a widely implemented interface is also much broader than naming one final class, because implementations participate in the friendship relationship.

Avoid
Do not summarize friendship as simply inherited or not inherited; the direction and which class is subclassed matter.
Construction invariants and meaningful test boundaries

Invalid dependencies are rejected before use. In the successful test, the input price is controlled but the discount rule itself executes.
Explain it: What defect should make the assertion fail, and which private access is actually necessary?
Limit: The 10-percent discount is an illustrative fixture, not an application rule. Friendship details and real integration require separate checks.

Read and verify

    Friendship is unilateral; distinguishes friends' subclasses from subclasses of the granting class.

column1: OODEEP-06 | Two references point to one resource-owning object. Does clearing one reference close the resource or destroy the object?
column2:
Short answer
Clearing one reference changes that variable to the null reference; another reference can still keep the object reachable. Memory reclamation by the garbage collector is distinct from business resource management. If a connection, registration, or lock needs timely release, I define an explicit ownership and release protocol and execute it on the relevant completion and failure paths.

Example
A coordinator and cache both hold a reference to the same session object. Clearing the coordinator's reference leaves the cache entry usable. An explicit close can be appropriate for the owner, but then other holders need defined behavior after closure, and a borrowed resource must not be closed accidentally.

Avoid
Reference clearing is not an object-level close operation and must not be used as a lock-release guarantee.
Value components versus a shared referent

Two structure values own independent string values but lead to the same pricing object. The arrow targets explain why a getter can expose mutable state.
Explain it: Which change affects only ls_copy, and which change affects an object visible through both?
Limit: Conceptual object identity, not physical memory addresses or a particular sharing optimization.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • Who may close a shared or borrowed object?
  • What should a second close or a call after close do?
Strong answer criteria
  • Separates reachability and resource lifetime
  • Identifies owner versus borrower
  • Defines closed-state behavior
Verification evidence
Tests cover multiple aliases, explicit close, repeated close, and use after closure.

    Initializing a reference is distinct from the garbage collector deleting an unreachable object.

column1: OODEEP-07 | An object can be created with a missing repository and fails much later on its first business call. What would you change?
column2:
Short answer
I make mandatory construction requirements explicit and establish a valid state before the object is usable. Constructor injection can require the repository, with a meaningful failure if the supplied reference is invalid. Complex or fallible setup can be coordinated by a factory. I avoid publishing a half-initialized object or making unrelated business operations depend on a hidden setup call.

Example
An approval service requires a repository and a policy. A public zero-argument constructor followed by set_repository creates an invalid intermediate state. Validate the mandatory dependencies at creation; if opening an external session is a separate lifecycle step, expose and test that lifecycle explicitly rather than surprising every constructor caller.

Avoid
Constructor injection does not validate an initial reference automatically, and heavy I/O is not required for good initialization.
Construction invariants and meaningful test boundaries

Invalid dependencies are rejected before use. In the successful test, the input price is controlled but the discount rule itself executes.
Explain it: What defect should make the assertion fail, and which private access is actually necessary?
Limit: The 10-percent discount is an illustrative fixture, not an application rule. Friendship details and real integration require separate checks.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • When would a factory improve error handling over constructor work?
  • How do you prevent this object escaping before setup succeeds?
Strong answer criteria
  • Defines construction invariants
  • Rejects missing dependencies early
  • Separates setup from business work
Verification evidence
Creation tests prove invalid dependencies fail immediately and valid instances need no undocumented setup call.

    Constructors establish initial state and can report construction failure.

column1: OODEEP-08 | A test passes alone but fails after another test changes CLASS-DATA. Why does NEW not reliably isolate it?
column2:
Short answer
Creating another instance initializes that instance's state; it does not reset class-level mutable state. Static attributes persist within the relevant internal session and may be shared by every instance of that class there. I identify and remove unnecessary global state or provide an explicit, controlled test reset. Cache keys and invalidation must also reflect the real context.

Example
One test loads a policy cache, then another expects changed customizing. Recreating the service leaves the static cache populated. An injected policy provider with test-owned lifetime can avoid this coupling; if caching is a genuine requirement, test refresh, invalidation, and relevant user or tenant context separately.

Avoid
CLASS-DATA is not per instance, but it is also not a globally synchronized cache across application servers.
Three distinct state and memory lifetimes

Empty row slots and the initial allocation are deliberately drawn separately. A new object does not imply a new internal session or empty class cache.
Explain it: Why can recreating a service leave a test-order failure unchanged?
Limit: Allocation diagram is qualitative; measure actual ABAP memory and cache lifetime in the target context.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • Does a class constructor rerun for every NEW?
  • Which context must appear in a security-sensitive cache key?
Strong answer criteria
  • Identifies static lifetime
  • Separates test isolation from construction
  • Defines cache scope and invalidation
Verification evidence
The suite passes individually, together, and with varied order without stale shared state.

column1: OODEEP-09 | A repository raises a low-level exception. Should a business service catch CX_ROOT and return an empty result?
column2:
Short answer
Usually not: an empty result can turn technical failure into a false business fact. I catch failures at a boundary that can recover or translate them into the service's declared meaning. When wrapping an exception, I preserve the original through previous so diagnosis remains possible. Expected absence, business rejection, and technical failure need distinguishable outcomes.

Example
A pricing repository connection failure must not look like 'no price exists' and trigger a free item. Translate the unavailable dependency into a meaningful service error while retaining its cause. Test not-found separately from unavailable, and ensure failure does not leave a misleading success result.

Avoid
Broad catch-and-default handling is not resilience when it changes an unknown outcome into valid-looking data.
Exceptional exits and preserved causes

The table names three exit paths that require separate reasoning. The exception chain carries the lower-level diagnosis through a meaningful service-level failure.
Explain it: Which path would a test of only propagated exceptions miss?
Limit: Simplified non-resumable scenarios; exact nesting and handlers determine CLEANUP execution. Resource ownership remains application-specific.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • When is catching CX_ROOT justified at an application boundary?
  • What information belongs in user feedback versus technical diagnostics?
Strong answer criteria
  • Keeps absence distinct from failure
  • Translates at an abstraction boundary
  • Preserves causal exception
Verification evidence
Tests assert distinct not-found and technical-failure paths, including the previous exception chain.

    Exception propagation and previous preserve a technical cause during translation.

column1: OODEEP-10 | A getter returns a reference to a mutable internal collection. Has private visibility protected the object's invariants?
column2:
Short answer
Private storage alone is insufficient if the getter hands out a reference that lets callers mutate the same data or object. I define whether the return value is a snapshot, a read capability, or intentionally shared mutable state. For an invariant-bearing aggregate, I prefer operations that validate changes and expose appropriate values rather than unrestricted aliases to internals.

Example
A cart validates positive item quantities in add_item, but get_items returns a writable data reference to its actual table. A caller can then insert a negative quantity without calling add_item. Returning a table value removes that table alias; reference components inside its rows still require separate ownership decisions.

Avoid
A copied reference is not a copied referent; changing the static view alone does not create immutable state.
Value components versus a shared referent

Two structure values own independent string values but lead to the same pricing object. The arrow targets explain why a getter can expose mutable state.
Explain it: Which change affects only ls_copy, and which change affects an object visible through both?
Limit: Conceptual object identity, not physical memory addresses or a particular sharing optimization.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • Does returning a table value solve reference components inside its rows?
  • Which mutation should remain an operation of the owning object?
Strong answer criteria
  • Finds alias-based invariant bypass
  • Chooses explicit ownership semantics
  • Considers nested references
Verification evidence
Attempted external mutation cannot bypass the owner's quantity rule or alter a promised snapshot.

    Reference assignment preserves the same object; static views do not clone mutable state.

column1: OODEEP-11 | A widely used provider interface needs an optional new capability. How do you avoid forcing unrelated implementations into fake behavior?
column2:
Short answer
I assess both callers and implementers before extending the contract. A separate capability interface may let interested clients request the new operation without requiring every existing provider to pretend it supports it. If the main interface must evolve, I define semantics, compatibility, and rollout deliberately. A no-op implementation is valid only when doing nothing genuinely satisfies the documented contract.

Example
A price provider gains simulation support, but one external provider cannot simulate. Adding simulate everywhere and returning an empty success hides a capability gap. A simulation interface and explicit capability selection can keep pricing callers unchanged; tests verify unsupported capability handling at the composition boundary.

Avoid
Adding a method is not automatically harmless merely because existing callers do not invoke it.
A concrete counterexample to substitutability

A valid quantity-one call exposes a behavioral violation invisible in matching parameter types. The lower table separates redefinition from a genuinely new capability.
Explain it: Would downcasting every caller to Provider B repair the contract? What else besides accepted inputs must agree?
Limit: Hypothetical contract; a narrower published domain would lead to a different assessment. No executable interface is implied.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • How will existing implementers activate after the interface change?
  • When would a separate version be clearer than optional capability discovery?
Strong answer criteria
  • Assesses caller and implementer impact
  • Avoids fake successful behavior
  • Defines migration and unsupported capability
Verification evidence
An implementation inventory and compatibility tests cover old clients and providers without simulation.

column1: OODEEP-12 | An OO unit test mocks calculate_total and then asserts the mocked total. What behavior has it proved?
column2:
Short answer
It has mainly proved the test configuration, not the calculation. I keep the behavior named as the code under test real and replace dependencies that make its inputs unpredictable, such as a price source or clock. Then I assert independently expected results and important failure behavior. A separate orchestration test may mock a calculator only when orchestration, rather than arithmetic, is its subject.

Example
To test a discount calculation, provide controlled prices and exercise the real calculation at the threshold and around it. To test whether checkout requests a calculation before posting, the calculator can be a collaborator double. Naming the test's responsibility makes that difference explicit.

Avoid
The same component can be a real subject in one test and a doubled dependency in another; coverage alone does not settle test quality.
Construction invariants and meaningful test boundaries

Invalid dependencies are rejected before use. In the successful test, the input price is controlled but the discount rule itself executes.
Explain it: What defect should make the assertion fail, and which private access is actually necessary?
Limit: The 10-percent discount is an illustrative fixture, not an application rule. Friendship details and real integration require separate checks.

  • What real integration evidence remains necessary after a double-based unit test?

  • Doubles only dependencies
  • Uses independent assertions

    Doubles isolate dependencies; the application scenario distinguishes a dependency from the behavior being tested.

column1: PAT-01 | Approval rules vary by country, while the application workflow should remain stable. Strategy or Template Method?
column2:
Short answer
Prefer an injected Strategy when approval calculation is the variation and the caller should select or replace it without changing its own class hierarchy. Template Method fits a deliberately stable algorithm skeleton with controlled subclass extension steps. Here, I would keep workflow coordination separate from country rules and pass explicit context to the selected rule. Inheritance becomes justified only if its protected extension contract and lifecycle are genuinely stable requirements.

Example
A country rule should return a decision rather than commit, send email or modify hidden global state. Test the same coordinator with several rule implementations. If countries also vary the process sequence, revisit the workflow model instead of adding increasingly powerful hooks that subclasses can use to violate invariants.

Avoid
Choosing inheritance solely to share code, or allowing a rule implementation to take over transaction ownership.
Strategy versus Template Method in approval rules

The same 700 EUR request receives different policy decisions through the same Strategy contract. Template Method instead fixes a call skeleton and exposes deliberate subclass steps.
Explain it: Which part varies, who selects it, and which object keeps transaction ownership?
Limit: Conceptual pattern comparison, not executable ABAP or a universal approval rule. Framework-owned construction may require a supported delegation seam.

Interviewer follow-ups
  • Which variation changes at runtime rather than through subclassing?
  • How would you prevent a new rule from changing the workflow's transaction boundary?
Strong answer criteria
  • Separates algorithm variation from coordination
  • Defends composition versus inheritance contextually
  • Keeps rules substitutable and independently testable

column1: PAT-02 | A posting integration needs matching serializer and sender implementations for each provider. Is one static factory sufficient?
column2:
Short answer
A simple factory can centralize selection for a small fixed set of implementations. Abstract Factory becomes useful when callers must obtain a compatible family, such as a provider-specific serializer and sender, without mixing families. I would choose the smallest construction design that protects the actual compatibility rule, rather than calling every method returning an object the Factory Method pattern.

Example
For two stable providers, an explicit factory returning a validated pair may suffice. If multiple related products evolve independently, a provider-factory interface can make their compatibility visible. Confusing a static creation helper with inheritance-based Factory Method or introducing an Abstract Factory for one trivial object.

column1: PAT-03 | A legacy posting API has awkward parameters and a three-step prepare/check/post sequence. Would you build an Adapter, a Facade, or both?
column2:
Short answer
Use an Adapter to translate the application's posting contract into the legacy API's types, identities and error representation. A Facade can expose a coherent business operation over the three underlying steps. They may coexist, but their boundaries must preserve authorization, failure information and transaction ownership. Neither pattern makes an unreleased API eligible for ABAP Cloud use or removes a nested commit. I would reject a superficially clean wrapper that hides those constraints.

Example
Separate mapping tests from orchestration tests. For example, verify that a zero amount remains explicit, API warnings do not become unconditional success, and a failed check prevents posting. Expose an uncertain remote outcome distinctly from a definitive rejection so callers can reconcile instead of duplicating work.

Avoid
Treating any wrapper as both a supported API and a transaction adapter without inspecting its dependencies.

column1: PAT-04 | You want timing, diagnostic logging and retries around an outbound service. Would stacked Decorators be safe?
column2:
Short answer
Decorators can add behavior around the same service interface without creating subclasses for every combination. I would make order explicit and preserve the wrapped contract, especially exceptions, authorization context and return values. Retrying is not a harmless decoration: it requires operation-specific idempotency and classification of uncertain outcomes. I would enable retries only where the service contract supports them, and decide whether timing and logging describe each attempt or the overall logical operation.

Example
A logging decorator outside a retry decorator records one logical call; inside it, it can observe individual attempts. Both can be useful if correlated clearly. Redact sensitive payloads and ensure diagnostic failure does not silently change a successful business result unless the required audit contract explicitly demands that behavior.

column1: PAT-05 | Three handlers can route a request to an approver. The first matching rule should win. How would you implement and test Chain of Responsibility?
column2:
Short answer
Model the decision contract explicitly: handled, not applicable and failed are different outcomes. An ordered Chain of Responsibility fits first-match routing when each handler can accept the request or pass it onward. Validate configuration order and define the no-match outcome. If the business instead needs every validation result, use an explicit validation pipeline or collection rather than stopping at the first successful handler and assuming the rest of the checks ran.

Example
Put the most specific route ahead of a general fallback only when that precedence is intended. Avoid hidden database writes in a routing handler; return a decision that the transaction coordinator applies. Log the rule identity so support can explain why the request reached a particular approver.

Avoid
Treating an exception as 'not applicable', or confusing first-match routing with execute-all validation.

column1: PAT-06 | A local ABAP event updates an ALV, and the team proposes another handler to start an external workflow. What boundary has changed?
column2:
Short answer
The local Observer arrangement is suitable for notifying listeners in the current execution context. Starting a durable external workflow introduces commit, delivery, retry and recovery requirements that an ordinary ABAP Objects event does not supply. I would keep local display notification separate from a committed business transition and use an appropriate transactional publication mechanism for the integration. Multiple listeners also require an explicit policy for exceptions and lifecycle registration.

Example
Registering multiple listener instances, failing to deregister obsolete listeners, or retaining state across tests can produce surprising local notifications. For the workflow, duplicate delivery and delayed events require durable consumer correlation and state checks. Do not infer asynchronous durability merely because the publisher does not directly name the receiving class.

Avoid
Assuming SET HANDLER creates a durable subscription or that Observer guarantees exactly-once business effects.

A registered local handler can update an ALV, while an external process needs transactional publication and durable processing evidence. Session-shared mutable state is a separate source of repeated-test failures.

column1: PAT-07 | A command object represents Submit and can be queued or retried. Does using Command make execution idempotent or undoable?
column2:
Short answer
No. Command packages an operation and its inputs; durability, authorization, idempotency and compensation are additional contracts. I would assign a stable business operation identity, decide how it is stored with the state transition, and define responses to repeated execution or conflicting payload reuse. An undo method is only meaningful where a valid inverse exists. A posted document may require a compensating business operation rather than deletion or an in-memory rollback.

Example
A command held only in memory is not a reliable job queue. When persistence is required, store a versioned data contract and reconstruct an eligible executor; do not treat an arbitrary object reference as a durable payload. Recheck the relevant authorization and business state at execution time.

Avoid
Assuming execute can safely run twice or that every business command has an exact inverse.

column1: PAT-08 | A repository interface improves testability, but its RAP implementation reads managed persistence directly. What can go wrong?
column2:
Short answer
The seam may be useful while the implementation is transactionally incorrect. A direct table read can miss creates, updates and deletes still in the RAP buffer. Define whether the repository contract means persisted state or the current transactional view; for transaction-sensitive BO logic, use the appropriate EML behavior access. Do not add a generic repository that writes managed tables and bypasses RAP checks. Test doubles must reproduce the relevant contract, not merely return convenient rows.

Example
A reporting query and a validation inside a modify flow can legitimately need different read semantics. Give those contracts distinct names or responsibilities. Test an update followed by a read before save, plus create and delete cases; an isolated unit test alone will not reveal a wrong persistence shortcut.

Avoid
Equating a mockable interface with correct behavior or recreating RAP's transactional buffer in a second general-purpose cache.

column1: PAT-09 | A singleton caches the current approver and makes tests pass alone but fail as a suite. How do you redesign its lifetime?
column2:
Short answer
I would remove request-specific mutable state from the singleton and make dependencies explicit. A conventional ABAP singleton is scoped to its internal session, not to all users or the whole landscape, and its lifetime can exceed one test or business operation. Prefer a freshly constructed, context-aware service or a cache with explicit key, scope and invalidation. If a shared instance is justified, specify immutability or cleanup rules and provide deterministic substitution in tests.

Caching the 'current user' implicitly is particularly dangerous for reusable jobs or delegated processing. Passing business context into the operation makes the dependency visible. column1: PAT-10 | A service obtains every dependency from a global factory inside its methods. How would you introduce dependency injection without building a framework?

Framework-owned classes may constrain construction, so create a small delegated application service or use a supported seam instead of inventing framework constructor parameters. column1: SQL-01 | How do ABAP SQL, Native SQL, CDS, and AMDP differ?
column2:
Short answer
ABAP SQL provides database access integrated with ABAP types and supported platform semantics. CDS defines reusable data models with additional semantics. Native SQL exposes database-specific capabilities with more responsibility on the developer. AMDP manages database procedures through ABAP repository objects, commonly using SQLScript on HANA. I choose the simplest supported option that meets the requirement.

Example
A filtered aggregate usually needs ABAP SQL or CDS, not a database procedure. A complex HANA-specific operation may justify AMDP after measurement. Release availability, client handling, authorization, and dependency release status must be checked for the chosen path.

Avoid
ABAP syntax around an AMDP method does not turn its SQLScript body into ABAP SQL or automatically apply CDS access control.

column1: SQL-02 | What is the empty-table trap in FOR ALL ENTRIES?
column2:
Short answer
If the driver internal table is empty, FOR ALL ENTRIES can cause the WHERE condition to be ignored and read all rows in scope. I guard the selection with a nonempty check and define the empty-input result explicitly. I also consider duplicate driver values, result duplicate elimination, and whether a join expresses the requirement better.

Example
For lt_customer_ids, an empty input should usually produce an empty result rather than all customers. Deduplicating repeated driver keys can reduce work. Because duplicate result rows are eliminated, omitting distinguishing columns may collapse records the application intended to keep separate.

Avoid
An empty FAE driver does not mean no rows; a separate filter in the same WHERE clause is not a safe replacement for the guard.

column1: SQL-03 | When would you use a join instead of FOR ALL ENTRIES?
column2:
Short answer
I favor a join when related database sources and their matching rules can be expressed clearly in one set-based operation. FOR ALL ENTRIES can be useful when driver data already exists in ABAP and the release or access constraints support it. Neither is universally faster; I compare semantics, transferred rows, buffering, and the measured execution plan.

Example
An order-to-item join naturally returns one row per matching item, while FAE may eliminate duplicates. If the caller needs orders only, EXISTS or a suitable projection may express the requirement more directly. Benchmark realistic volumes, including sparse and skewed keys.

Avoid
Replacing FAE with a join can change duplicates and row counts even when the new query runs faster.

column1: SQL-04 | How can a LEFT OUTER JOIN accidentally behave like an inner join?
column2:
Short answer
A left outer join preserves unmatched left rows and supplies NULL for the missing right side. A WHERE condition requiring a right-side value can reject those unmatched rows. If the condition belongs to matching, I put it in ON; if it is intended to filter the final result, WHERE may be correct.

Example
To list every order with its optional English description, the language condition often belongs in ON. Putting description-language equals English in WHERE can remove orders with no matching description. The intended business result determines placement, not a mechanical rule.

Avoid
Moving conditions between ON and WHERE is not always semantics-preserving for outer joins.

column1: SQL-05 | What is the difference between SQL NULL and an ABAP initial value?
column2:
Short answer
NULL represents missing or unknown SQL information; an ABAP initial value is a defined value for its type. SQL predicates use three-valued logic, so comparison to NULL does not behave like comparison to zero or an empty string. I use IS NULL, COALESCE, or supported null indicators when the distinction matters.

Example
After an outer join, a missing amount and a real zero amount are different business facts. Plain transfer into an ABAP field can make both appear initial unless the query or result handling preserves the distinction deliberately.

Avoid

column1: SQL-06 | How do GROUP BY, WHERE, and HAVING work together?
column2:
Short answer
WHERE selects input rows before grouping. GROUP BY defines the groups, and aggregate expressions calculate a result per group. HAVING filters those groups using group-level conditions. I push suitable filtering and aggregation to the database while preserving currency, unit, and join semantics, rather than moving a large raw dataset to ABAP unnecessarily.

Example
For sales totals by company and currency, first restrict the posting period, group by company and currency, then apply a threshold to each total. Joining items to several partners before summing may multiply each item amount and produce an inflated total.

Database aggregation is not automatically correct if different currencies are mixed or joins multiply the rows being aggregated.

column2:
Short answer
I first establish the correct result and a reproducible baseline. Then I inspect unnecessary rows and columns, repeated calls, missing filters, costly joins, and excessive round trips. I prefer reducing work at the data source before micro-optimizing ABAP expressions. Each change is measured with representative data and checked for unchanged business semantics.

Example
A loop issuing one SELECT for each of thousands of items may spend time on repeated database calls. A set-based fetch can help, but it must preserve authorization and transaction consistency. Fetching every column or an unbounded result can dominate memory and transfer cost.

Avoid
A query that is fast on ten development rows may be unsuitable for millions of production rows or a different key distribution.
